text:
The Exaltation of the Holy Cross by Father Francis Xavier Weninger, DD, SJ, 1876.
.
This festival was instituted in commemoration of the day on which the holy Cross of Christ, was, with great solemnities, brought back to Jerusalem. Chosroes, king of Persia, had invaded Syria with a powerful army, and had conquered Jerusalem, the capital. He caused the massacre of eighty thousand men, and also took many prisoners away with him, among whom was the Patriarch Zachary. But more painful than all this to the Christians was, that he carried away the holy, Cross of our Saviour, which, after great pains, had been discovered by the holy empress, St. Helena. The pagan king carried it with him to Persia, adorned it magnificently with pearls and precious stones, and placed it upon the top of his royal throne of pure gold. Thus was the holy Cross held in higher honor by the heathen king, than Martin Luther would have manifested; for, in one of his sermons, he says of it: "If a piece of the holy Cross were given to me and I had it in my hand, I would soon put it where the sun would never shine on it."
.
Heraclius, the pious emperor, was greatly distressed at this misfortune, and as he had not an army sufficiently large to meet so powerful an enemy, he made propositions for peace. Chosroes, inflated by many victories, refused at first to listen to the emperor's proposal, but at length consented, on condition that Heraclius should forsake the faith of Christ and worship the Sun, the god of the Persians. Indignant at so wicked a request, the emperor, seeing that it was a question of religion, concerning the honor of the Most High, broke off all negotiation with his impious enemy. Taking refuge in prayer, he assembled all the Christian soldiers of his dominions, and commanded all his subjects to appease the wrath of the Almighty, and ask for His assistance, by fasting, praying, giving alms and other good works. He himself gave them the example. After this, he went courageously, with his comparatively small army, to meet the haughty Chosroes, having given strict orders that his soldiers, besides abstaining from other vices, should avoid all plundering and blaspheming, that they might prove themselves worthy of the divine assistance.
.
Taking a crucifix in his hand, he animated his soldiers by pointing towards it, saying they should consider for whose honor they were fighting, and that there was nothing more glorious than to meet death for the honor of God and His holy religion. Thus strengthened, the Christian army marched against the enemy. Three times were they attacked by three divisions of the Persian army, each one led by an experienced general; and three times they repulsed the enemy, so that Chosroes himself had at last to flee. His eldest son, Siroes, whom he had excluded from the succession to the throne, seized the opportunity, and not only assassinated his own father, but also his brother, Medarses, who had been chosen by Chosroes as his associate and successor. To secure the crown which he had thus forcibly seized, Siroes offered peace to Heraclius, restored to him the conquered provinces, and also sent back the holy Cross, the patriarch Zachary, and all the other prisoners of war. Heraclius, in great joy, hastened with the priceless wood to Jerusalem, to offer due thanks to the Almighty for the victory, and to restore the holy Cross, which the Persians had kept in their possession during fourteen years, to its former place.
.
All the inhabitants of the city, the clergy and laity, came to meet the pious emperor. The latter had resolved to carry the Cross to Mount Calvary, to the church fitted up for its reception. A solemn procession was formed, in which the Patriarch, the courtiers and an immense multitude of people took part. The clergy preceded, and the emperor, arrayed in sumptuous robes of state, carried the holy Cross upon his shoulder. Having thus passed through the city, they came to the gate that leads to Calvary, when suddenly the emperor stood still and could not move from the spot. At this miracle, all became frightened, not knowing what to think of it. Only to St. Zachary did God reveal the truth. Turning to the emperor the patriarch said: "Christ was not arrayed in splendor when He bore His Cross through this gate. His brow was not adorned with a golden crown, but with one made of thorns. Perhaps, O emperor, your magnificent robe is the cause of your detention."
.
The pious Heraclius humbly gave ear to the words of the patriarch, divested himself of his imperial purple, and put on poor apparel, he took the crown from his head and the shoes from his feet. Having done this, the sacred treasure was again laid on his shoulder: when, behold! nothing detained him, and he carried it to the place of its destination. The holy patriarch then deposited the Cross in its former place, and duly venerated it with all who were present. God manifested how much He was pleased with the honor they had paid to the holy Cross of Christ, by many miracles wrought on the same day. A dead man was restored to life by being touched by the sacred wood; four paralytic persons obtained the use of their limbs; fifteen who were blind received sight; many sick recovered their health; and several possessed were freed from the devil by devoutly touching it.
.
PRACTICAL CONSIDERATIONS.
.
I. The Cross on which Christ had died was raised and greatly honored by all the faithful. I suppose that if you possessed a particle of the true Cross, you would greatly honor and cherish it. But why do you not love and honor that cross, those trials which God sends you? They are, in a spiritual sense, a particle of the Cross of Christ, which will be most beneficial to you, if you bear it patiently. Christ, the Lord, called His crucifixion an exaltation, saying: "The Son of Man must be exalted; "because by it He was exalted in heaven and on earth, as He bore His sufferings and His death out of love for His heavenly Father and for the salvation of men. You also will be exalted in heaven, if, in carrying your cross, you follow the example of Christ. Many carry their crosses, like the thief on the left of Christ, with murmuring and impatience, others, like the one on His right, with patience and resignation, knowing that they deserve them. Jesus carried His Cross not only with patience, but, according to the words of the Apostle, with joy, although He was innocent. With whom do you carry yours? With whom will you carry it in future? If you carry it with the first, you will not be exalted, but precipitated into the depth of hell.

Hangzhou Open (ATP 250)

 Kyrian Jacquet vs Tomas Martin Etcheverry

Round of 16 · Outdoor hard · 07:30 local

🧠 Form & Context

Kyrian Jacquet

📈 The raw form lead: His CFS is 61.1 against 50.8, a 10.3-point advantage despite an even 5–5 last ten.

🎾 A surface number that needs context: His last-52-week ATP hard record is only 2–4. The 71.4% blended hard figure (20–8) relies heavily on Challenger and ITF results, so it is not a validated ATP-level edge.

✅ A useful local result: He came through a completed three-set opener against Aleksandar Vukic, 7–6(5), 3–6, 6–3.

⚠️ The class and durability tests: He is 0–3 against top-50 opponents over the last 52 weeks. His 2026 collapse rate is 24.1% (7/29), and the supplied history records three retirements across the recent seasons.

Tomas Martin Etcheverry

🏆 The stronger tour-level résumé: A maiden ATP title in 2026 and a 13–0 last-52-week record against players outside the top 100 give him a clear class argument.

📉 No commanding hard-court form: His last-52-week ATP hard record stands at 12–13; his last ten overall is also 5–5.

🕒 A rhythm question: The supplied review flags a 19-day break since his last hard-court match. That makes the early start an additional uncertainty.

🔒 Better lead protection: His 2026 collapse rate is 19.0% (4/21), compared with Jacquet's 24.1%. Neither number settles the matchup alone.

🔍 Match Breakdown

Jacquet has a real route to competing: he has already played and won a tight match at this venue, while Etcheverry brings an extended break and a merely even recent ATP hard record. A long match would allow Jacquet's current rhythm and overall results to matter.

The central limitation is the level behind Jacquet's surface score. His 20–8 blended hard record includes a large lower-tier contribution, whereas Etcheverry's opposition profile and ATP title offer a firmer measure of performance at this level. Jacquet's weak top-50 return and higher collapse rate keep us from treating the 10.3-point CFS lead as a clean underdog endorsement. The first set should tell us more about Etcheverry's sharpness than the raw ranking gap does.

🔮 Prediction

Etcheverry has the stronger route through class and lead protection, but his hard-court record and time away leave space for Jacquet to make this competitive.

text:
You've got the causation exactly backwards, so let's fix that first and then get to who actually approved these taxes.

California isn't expensive because it needs money. 

It's expensive because 39 million people and half the world's tech industry want to live in the same 100 miles of coastline and bid the housing up. 

The gap between California and Texas in taxes is a few percentage points of income. 

You said: "They can't fund themselves" 

California sends about $650 billion a year to Washington and gets less back per person than it pays. 

It funds itself and Mississippi. The states that literally can't fund themselves without money from somewhere else are the ones getting $1.50 to $2.00 back per dollar. 

You've described the donor as the dependent.

Now the part you'll like least: Californians keep voting for these taxes. 

On purpose. By name.

Prop 30 (2012) — the 13.3% top income tax rate on millionaires. Voters passed it 55–45. Prop 55 (2016) extended it to 2030 — passed 63–37. Marin, San Francisco, and Santa Clara — where the millionaires actually live — voted yes.

Prop 63 (2004) — the 1% millionaire's tax for mental health. Voter-approved.

Prop 56 (2016) — $2-a-pack tobacco tax. 64% yes.
Prop 6 (2018) — a ballot measure to repeal the gas tax increase. Voters rejected the repeal 57–43. They were offered lower gas taxes and said no thanks.

Measure M (2016) — LA County's half-cent transit sales tax. 71% yes. Measure H (2017), the homelessness sales tax — 69% yes.

Props 1 and 2 (2024) — $6.4 billion mental health bond and $10 billion school bond. Both passed.

And it cuts the other way, which is the point: California voters can reject taxes and do. 

Prop 13 (1978) capped property taxes at 1% and required a two-thirds legislative vote for any state tax increase — the strictest anti-tax rule in the country, still in force. 

Prop 30 (2022), a new tax on income over $2 million, went down 58–42. 

Every local sales tax, parcel tax, and school bond in California has to go on a ballot. 

This is the hardest state in the country to raise a tax in without asking the people paying it — which means every tax you're calling "extreme" is one that survived a public vote.

True democracy. 

So the picture isn't a state "held up" by taxes it extracts from unwilling citizens. 

It's the fourth-largest economy on Earth whose residents periodically walk into a booth and vote to tax themselves to pay for transit, schools, and mental health, and periodically vote not to when they think it's too much. 

That's not a failed state. That's the thing the founders called self-government, working roughly as designed, in a place rich enough to afford it.

Maybe broke ass Red Sates could learn alot from th 4th largest economy in the world.

text:
Fine as silk and woven into a delicate, lacy sheet, Khanom La is more than a Southern Thai sweet. Behind every strand is a tradition passed down through generations.

1️⃣🌾 The Art of Making Khanom La
At its heart, Khanom La is made with just two essentials: flour and sugar. The flour is usually a blend of rice flour with tapioca starch or glutinous rice flour, while the sweetness comes from a carefully balanced mix of nipa palm sugar and palmyra palm sugar.
Making it takes a practiced hand. The batter is drizzled in fine strands over a hot pan, with careful control of both rhythm and heat, until the strands come together in a thin, delicate sheet resembling woven fabric.

2️⃣🙏 A Sweet with a Special Meaning
Khanom La is one of five traditional sweets used to prepare a Mrup, a set of offerings presented to Buddhist monks during the Tenth Lunar Month merit-making tradition and dedicated to departed ancestors. Its delicate, cloth-like appearance symbolizes clothing offered to ancestors, reflecting family bonds, remembrance, and gratitude.

3️⃣🐚 Where to Find It: Ban Hoi Rak
One of Pak Phanang’s best-known Khanom La-making communities is Ban Hoi Rak, now known as Ban Si Sombun, in Pak Phanang District, Nakhon Si Thammarat. Here, the tradition continues from one generation to the next.

4️⃣✨ From Tradition to a Mueang Khon Favorite
Khanom La is no longer reserved for the festival season. Today, you can find it year-round, from traditional soft sheets to crispy La Krop, making it a favorite souvenir from Nakhon Si Thammarat.

Next time you’re in Mueang Khon, as Nakhon Si Thammarat is affectionately known, make a stop for Khanom La after paying respect to the sacred Phra That at Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan. Taste it fresh, then take a few packs home to share.

A hidden camera caught Southern Methodist University staffer Danielle Palomo saying the quiet part out loud. "As you can probably imagine, we've had to do a lot of maneuvering in order to remain kind of hidden under a lot of things," Palomo told an undercover journalist with Accuracy In Media. "But as long as we can keep doing what we're doing even to a smaller capacity, that is what we're gonna do."

Palomo, SMU's "Coordinator for Community Engagement, Social Change and Intercultural Engagement," laid out exactly how the university dodged its own supposed DEI wind-down: the Office of Diversity and Inclusion never closed — it was simply renamed the Office of Cultural Intelligence and kept running under the new label.

SMU's media director, Megan Jacob, told The College Fix the exact opposite. "SMU does not operate a hidden DEI program," she said, insisting the school "does offer activities under the Cultural Intelligence framework" adopted back in 2017 — the very framework Palomo just described as cover. Palomo did not respond to two emails asking her to explain the contradiction.

Accuracy In Media president Adam Guillette isn't buying the rebrand. "No taxpayer, donor, or student should be forced to fund this divisive, hateful activism," he said, calling on SMU to hire an independent investigator to root DEI out of its programs and curriculum. SMU is private, but it still takes federal funding — and Texas law bans DEI at public universities for exactly the kind of maneuvering Palomo just confessed to on tape.

This isn't AIM's first catch. A University of Missouri staffer was suspended weeks ago after being caught the same way, and a Western Carolina University administrator was recorded admitting DEI is alive and well despite a system-wide ban. Three schools, three denials, three hidden-camera confessions — the pattern isn't a coincidence, it's a strategy.

text:
Happy Birthday Christopher Reeve

The one and only Superman, an exceptional actor and a first rate human being, Reeve was born in New York to Barbara Pitney Lamb and Franklin D'Olier Reeve. His parents divorced in 1956, and the young Christopher moved to Princeton, New Jersey, where he attended Princeton Day School. Reeve excelled academically, athletically, and onstage; he was on the honor roll and played soccer, baseball, and tennis and was adept at the piano. He attended Cornell University, and in 1975, auditioned for the Broadway play “A Matter of Gravity.” Katharine Hepburn watched his audition and cast him as her character's grandson. Reeve and Hepburn became very close and some gossip columnists even claimed they were having an affair. Reeve said, "She was 67 and I was 22, but I thought that it was quite an honour!” In 1976, the actor was asked to audition for the role of Clark Kent in the big-budget film “Superman” (1978). A meeting with the director was arranged, and the morning after, Reeve was sent a 300-page script of surprising intelligence, and was told that Marlon Brando was going to play Jor-Eland, and Gene Hackman Lex Luthor. The actor later said, "By the late 1970s, the masculine image had changed….Now it was acceptable for a man to show gentleness and vulnerability….I felt that the new Superman ought to reflect that contemporary male image." He based his portrayal of Kent on Cary Grant in the 1938 film “Bringing Up Baby”. The ridiculously handsome Reeve, a throwback to old Hollywood, was tall but skinny and went through a two-month training regimen with former British weightlifting champion David Prowse, adding 30 pounds of muscle to his 188 pound frame. “Superman” grossed $300.2 million worldwide and Reeve received considerable acclaim for his performance. (His last movie in the franchise was the disappointing “Superman IV: The Quest for Peace”, 1987. It was a critical failure and a box-office flop. Reeve later commented, "the less said about it the better.") His next film was the wonderful 1980 time-travel romance, “Somewhere in Time”, co-starring Christopher Plummer and Jane Seymour. It was Reeve’s personal favourite and has become a cult classic. In 1982, he played a novice playwright in Sidney Lumet's dark comedy “Deathtrap,” opposite Michael Caine. The same year, he gave a commanding performance as a corrupt Catholic priest in “Monsignor”. Reeve was delighted when he was offered the meaty role of Basil Ransom in Merchant Ivory’s “The Bostonians.” The film exceeded expectations and performed exceptionally well at the box office. The New York Times called it “among the finest film adaptations of a classic novel that anyone has yet made." Ivory thought that Reeve was "so intelligent and wonderful" in it, but "really undervalued by the critics because they were so used to thinking of him as Superman." In 1985, against Katherine Hepburn’s eerily prescient advice, Reeve made the tragic mistake of starring in the television film “Anna Karenina.” It was for this production that Reeve learned to ride and decided to take up the sport professionally. In the spring of 1992, he attended the US premiere of “Howards End” where he met James Ivory once more, who offered him a role in his new film, “The Remains of the Day” (1993). It became an instant classic. Ivory praised Reeve again, saying, "He was a great, great  guy... a very, very good actor.” In 1995, Reeve became paralysed after his horse crashed into a jump at a cross-country competition. Stoical and devoid of self-pity, he continued to work as best as he could, and in 1998, published an autobiography, “Still Me.” His final acting role was in the television series “Smallville.” By early October 2004, Reeve was being treated for an infected pressure ulcer that was causing sepsis. On October 9, the actor went into cardiac arrest and fell into a coma. Eighteen hours later, Reeve died, aged 52.

text:
“You Can’t Go To Court If Someone Enters A Temple And Offers Namaz”
 - Vishnu Shankar Jain 

In hearings before the Madhya Pradesh High Court (Indore bench), Jain, representing Hindu petitioners, contended that the Bhojshala complex is historically a Sanskrit learning centre and temple site from Raja Bhoj’s Parmar era, and revenue/ASI records refer to it as “Bhojshala.”

Merely offering namaz at a place does not, by itself, convert that place into a mosque or make it Waqf property under law.

Therefore, the 2003 ASI order that permitted Friday namaz at the ASI-protected monument should not be treated as establishing the site’s legal character as a mosque.

The pithy phrasing “you can’t go to court if you enter a temple and offer namaz” captures this core idea: performing a religious act (namaz) inside a structure that is, on evidence, a temple does not automatically change its legal status or defeat the temple-side’s rights.

On 15 May 2026, the MP High Court delivered its verdict:

It declared the Bhojshala complex a temple and granted Hindus the right to worship there.

It partially/quashed the ASI’s 7 April 2003 order that had allowed Friday namaz at the site, holding that henceforth only Hindu worship would take place there.

It directed the state government to consider allotting separate land for a mosque and to consider the Hindu side’s request for repatriation of the Vagdevi idol from the UK.

Jain called the judgment “historic” and said the court had recognised the complex as belonging to Raja Bhoj and set aside the earlier namaz-permission order.

Jain’s argument was specific to the Bhojshala facts (historical records, ASI findings, continuity of Hindu worship, and the legal question of Waqf status). It does not mean that offering namaz anywhere can never have legal consequences; rather, in this case, the court accepted that namaz alone did not establish the site as a mosque or override the temple character established by other evidence.

Dear Jiaxian,
May this letter find you well.

On this Mid-Autumn Festival, beneath the full moon, I send you all the longing in my heart.

You were once a pure and open-hearted young man. Born into privilege, you dreamed of architecture, not for wealth or fame, but to use what you had learned to build a better world and see what lay beyond the horizon.

Then came that fleeting encounter on the opera stage.

You saved the woman you loved, and from that moment, you were determined to spend the rest of your life with her. Though your father disapproved, your second mother brought your younger siblings to offer their blessings.

For that brief moment, you believed you had finally found happiness.

But the dream was never meant to last.

Your father died suddenly. Your younger siblings disappeared under mysterious circumstances. Desperate and with nowhere left to turn, you abandoned your pride and sought help from everyone you could.

Only to watch your siblings die before your eyes. Only to watch your second mother take her own life.

You tried to follow them into death, sinking into the depths of the lake, hoping to sleep forever.

But fate brought you back to shore.

Overnight, your dreams were destroyed. Your family was gone. Your love was lost. And you were left to endure accusations, insults, and a life of humiliation on the streets.

In a desolate temple, a length of hemp rope and a pile of firewood witnessed your final struggle. The despair of being unable to die, the devastation of uncovering the truth behind the conspiracy, and the moment you swore to pursue revenge until the very end.

Now, the game of fate begins again.

You are me. I am you.

I am Shangguan Chengming—the man who buried your innocent past and began a second life.

We did it. And yet, more than anything, I wish it had all been an illusion.

I wish you were still that young man, full of hope, living with all the passion life had to offer.

— Shangguan Chengming

Religious Dress and Codes in Greek Culture
Yes — Greek culture had both ancient and later traditions of regulated dress for religious roles, including for women in sacred or monastic contexts, though there was no “nun” in the modern sense in antiquity.
Ancient Greek religious dress codes
In Classical and Hellenistic Greece, there were sacred laws (hieroi nomoi) in some sanctuaries that set rules for attire, hairstyles, jewelry, belts, and shoes for worshippers and cult officials 📷ResearchGate. These regulations often aimed to maintain purity, avoid ostentation, and ensure proper ritual conduct. For example, certain garments or adornments were prescribed for priestesses or other cult participants, and clothing could signal ritual status or role 📷Academia.edu+1.
Ancient Greek women’s clothing — such as the chiton and peplos — could be adapted for religious use, sometimes with specific colors, fabrics, or draping styles for cultic occasions 📷Wikipedia+1. There is no evidence of a formal “nun” order in antiquity, but priestesses and other female cult figures did have distinct dress codes.
Greek Orthodox monastic dress
In the Byzantine and modern Greek Orthodox tradition, there is a monastic habit worn by both male and female monks and nuns 📷https://t.co/jDWGhGZoXp. This habit is a visible marker of monastic identity and is tied to spiritual ideals, though the tradition holds that “the habit does not make the priest” — meaning the clothing is symbolic rather than the sole source of spiritual authority. The habit’s design, colors, and materials can vary by convent and tradition, and it is part of the socialization process into monastic life 📷https://t.co/jDWGhGZoXp.
Key points
Antiquity: No formal “nun” orders, but priestesses and cult women had regulated dress under sanctuary laws 📷Academia.edu+1.
Byzantine/Orthodox era: Female monastics wear a specific habit, part of a long tradition of monastic dress in the Eastern Christian world 📷

21 Your kerchiefs also will I tear, and deliver my people out of your hand, and they shall be no more in your hand to be hunted; and ye shall know that I am the Lord..
Purpose: In both periods, dress codes served to express piety, maintain ritual purity, and signal religious identity.
So, while there was no “nun” in the modern sense in ancient Greece, there were dress codes for women in religious roles, and in later Greek Orthodox tradition, nuns do have a defined habit and dress code.

Dress Code for Women Serving Baal
There is no surviving detailed description of a specific “dress code” for women serving Baal, but biblical and ancient Near Eastern sources indicate that Baal worshipers — including women — wore distinctive, uniform vestments set apart for ritual service, as seen in 2 Kings 10:22.
Biblical evidence
In 2 Kings 10:22, King Jehu orders the keeper of the wardrobe to “bring out garments for all the worshipers of Baal.” The text specifies that these were vestments — special garments reserved for the cultic service of Baal — and that they were kept in a dedicated wardrobe 📷Bible Hub+1. This shows that Baal worship had an organized system of attire, and that the garments were distinctive and uniform, marking the worshipers as part of the Baal cult and setting them apart from those serving Yahweh 📷Bible Hub.
While the verse does not specify gender, the “all the worshipers of Baal” phrase would have included both men and women. In the ancient Near East, women who served in temple or cultic roles often wore ceremonial clothing that signified their function and allegiance to the deity 📷Bible Hub.
Ancient Near Eastern context
In Mesopotamian and Canaanite religion, priestesses and other female cult participants frequently wore elaborate ceremonial garments — sometimes with symbolic colors, patterns, or accessories — that reflected the deity’s associations and the ritual’s nature 📷Wikipedia. These garments could be part of a standardized set, similar to the “vestments” mentioned in the Bible, and were used to unify the worship community visually.
Symbolism and function
According to biblical commentary, these vestments were not just functional but symbolic, representing the worshipers’ identity and loyalty to Baal 📷Bible Hub. The fact that Jehu targeted these garments in his reform shows how central they were to the cult’s organization and visibility.
Summary
No exact “dress code” list survives for women serving Baal.
Biblical record confirms the existence of special, uniform vestments for Baal worshipers, including women 📷Bible Hub+1.
Ancient Near Eastern practice suggests these were ceremonial, possibly gender-specific, and symbolically charged 📷Wikipedia.
The garments served to identify and unify the cult community, marking them as distinct from Israel’s covenant worshipers 📷Bible Hub.
In short, women serving Baal would have worn ritual vestments from a dedicated wardrobe, chosen to be distinctive and symbolic, though the exact style and details are not recorded in surviving texts.

Dress Code for Women Serving as Asherah
There is no surviving formal “dress code” for women serving as Asherah, but archaeological and biblical evidence shows they wore elaborate, symbolic garments—often veils and woven hangings—crafted for the goddess’s sacred poles (asherim) and ritual objects 📷Feminism and Religion+1.
What the sources say
In Canaanite and early Israelite religion, Asherah was honored through wooden poles or pillars (asherim) carved from trees, sometimes decorated with silver and gold, and placed in sacred spaces 📷Feminism and Religion+1.
Women played a central role in her worship:
They offered incense and liquid offerings and baked sweet cakes for the “Queen of Heaven” 📷Feminism and Religion.
They wove elaborate veils to dress the asherim 📷Feminism and Religion.
Biblical passages (e.g., 2 Kings 23:7) mention women weaving hangings or dresses for the Asherah, which were later destroyed during reforms 📷Christian Answers Network.
These garments were not everyday clothing but ritual textiles—likely richly decorated, possibly with symbolic motifs such as the Tree of Life, and intended to honor the goddess’s presence 📷Feminism and Religion+1.
No standardized “code”
The available evidence does not describe a fixed set of rules for women’s dress in Asherah service. Instead, the “dress code” appears to have been contextual and symbolic:
Veils and hangings were the most common elements, used to clothe the sacred pole or altar 📷Feminism and Religion+1.
The style and materials would have reflected the wealth, status, and religious tradition of the worshipper’s community.
The focus was on ritual purity and symbolic representation rather than a uniform style across all regions or times.
Summary
Women serving Asherah did not follow a single, codified dress code. Their attire was ritualistic and symbolic, centered on elaborate veils and woven hangings for the asherim, crafted with care and possibly adorned with precious materials, as part of a broader set of offerings and ceremonies 📷Feminism and Religion+1.

text:
Baal cult is foreign contamination, not an original or legitimate strand of Yahweh worship. 

The Levitical/Aaronic system is the one that absorbed or coexisted with that contamination after Israel settled in Canaan. The Melchizedek line is presented in the texts as older, non-hereditary, non-Levitical, and non-bloody in the only encounter recorded.

Baal as smuggled practice
The Hebrew texts treat Baal worship as apostasy and adultery against the covenant, not as a parallel or precursor that Yahweh later “took over.” Elijah’s contest, Hosea’s language of whoring after the Baals, Jeremiah’s insistence that burning children “to Baal” or Molech “never entered my mind,” and Josiah’s destruction of high places and the Tophet are framed as purification of something illicit that had entered the land. High places, asherah poles, fertility rites, and child-sacrifice episodes are repeatedly tied to Canaanite practice that Israelites adopted after entering the territory. Early use of “Baal” as a title meaning “lord” for Yahweh himself was later treated as dangerous precisely because it blurred the line. The prophetic complaint is that people kept Yahweh for crises while adding Baal for rain, crops, and local fertility—syncretism, not organic development. That is smuggling.

Storm imagery that later appears in psalms can be read as polemic expropriation (“Yahweh, not Baal, rides the clouds”) rather than shared origin. The texts themselves draw the line: Yahweh is not a dying-and-rising fertility god and does not accept the child offerings associated with Baal/Molech.

Two priesthoods
The Levitical/Aaronic priesthood is tribal, hereditary, and post-Sinai. It is instituted in Exodus–Numbers for Aaron and his sons from the tribe of Levi. Its core work is the tabernacle and later Temple cult: daily offerings, sin/purification offerings, the Day of Atonement blood ritual, and the explicit rationale in Leviticus 17:11 that life is in the blood and Yahweh has given it on the altar for *kipper*. This system is national, tied to the Mosaic covenant, and requires genealogical qualification. After settlement it operated at local high places as well as the central sanctuary—the same sites previously used for Canaanite worship. That is where the contamination occurred. The prophets attack empty or hypocritical use of this apparatus, not always the apparatus itself, but they never treat the blood rites as optional window-dressing.

Melchizedek appears earlier, in Genesis 14, before any Levitical institution exists. He is king of Salem and priest of El Elyon (“God Most High”). He brings bread and wine, blesses Abram, and receives a tithe. No animal is mentioned, no genealogy is given, no tribal restriction appears. Psalm 110 then swears an oath that a Davidic figure will be “priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.” Hebrews 5–7 makes the contrast systematic: Abraham (and therefore Levi still in his loins) paid tithe to Melchizedek and received blessing from him, so the earlier priesthood is greater; a change of priesthood requires a change of law; Jesus, from Judah, holds an eternal, non-hereditary office of this order and offers himself once rather than repeating animal blood. The Melchizedek figure is king *and* priest; the Levitical priests are not kings.

El Elyon in the Genesis encounter is the high God who owns heaven and earth. In the wider Canaanite milieu El is the senior deity and Baal is a younger storm/fertility figure. The biblical narrative identifies El Elyon with Yahweh for Abraham, while treating Baal as the rival that must be expelled. Melchizedek’s cult, as written, is therefore not Baal worship.

Sacrifice and later reception
The blood-atonement logic belongs to the Levitical/Priestly strand. It is not required in the Melchizedek encounter. Gnostic *Melchizedek* (Nag Hammadi) has the figure offer a “living offering” of himself and his offspring, explicitly contrasting it with cattle offered for sins of unbelief; bloody sacrifice is associated with Death and the archons. Origen treats Aaronic rites as shadow and Melchizedek/Christ as the reality, with bread and wine as the type of the Eucharist rather than animal slaughter. Coptic and Ethiopian liturgical use likewise cites Melchizedek’s bread and wine as prefiguring the unbloody offering. Hebrews uses the same contrast to argue the Levitical system could not perfect and has been set aside.

The Levitical blood cult is therefore the one that developed inside Israel after contact with Canaan and that later Christian and Gnostic writers relativized by appealing to the older Melchizedek model. Whether that older model was itself a Jebusite or El-cult survival later “Yahweh-ized” is a historical question the received texts do not concede; they present it as legitimate worship of the Most High before the Mosaic legislation.

Who acted against Jesus
The high priests who handed Jesus to Pilate were Levitical/Aaronic (Caiaphas and the Temple establishment). Their logic, as recorded, combined a blasphemy charge with Caiaphas’s political calculation that one man’s death was preferable to Roman destruction of the nation and the Temple order. Jesus is presented in the New Testament as operating in the Melchizedek line—an eternal priest-king outside the Aaronic genealogy. That claim, if taken seriously, implied the existing sacrificial and priestly apparatus was not final. The Temple authorities had institutional reason to see it as a threat. Romans supplied the actual execution for the political title “King of the Jews.” The Gnostic and some patristic readings relocate the real conflict to lower powers or treat the death as the moment the material body (associated with the lower creator) is discarded. The narrative sequence in the earliest sources remains Levitical leadership initiative followed by Roman sentence.

text:
Im SO tired of this stupid quote. 

Idiot…states like California aren’t expensive because it needs money. 

It's expensive because 39 million people and half the world's tech industry want to live in the same 100 miles of coastline and bid the housing up. 

The gap between California and Texas in taxes is a few percentage points of income. 

California sends about $650 billion a year to Washington and gets less back per person than it pays. 

It funds itself and Mississippi. The states that literally can't fund themselves without money from somewhere else are the ones getting $1.50 to $2.00 back per dollar. 

You are describing high tax states as dependent when they are the donors to broke ass red states.

Now the part you'll like least: 

Californians keep voting for these taxes. 

On purpose. By name.

Prop 30 (2012) — the 13.3% top income tax rate on millionaires. Voters passed it 55–45. 

Prop 55 (2016) extended it to 2030 — passed 63–37. Marin, San Francisco, and Santa Clara — where the millionaires actually live — voted yes.

Prop 63 (2004) — the 1% millionaire's tax for mental health. Voter-approved.

Prop 56 (2016) — $2-a-pack tobacco tax. 64% yes.

Prop 6 (2018) — a ballot measure to repeal the gas tax increase. Voters rejected the repeal 57–43. They were offered lower gas taxes and said no thanks.

Measure M (2016) — LA County's half-cent transit sales tax. 71% yes. 

Measure H (2017), the homelessness sales tax — 69% yes.

Props 1 and 2 (2024) — $6.4 billion mental health bond and $10 billion school bond. Both passed.

And it cuts the other way, which is the point: California voters can reject taxes and do. 

Prop 13 (1978) capped property taxes at 1% and required a two-thirds legislative vote for any state tax increase — the strictest anti-tax rule in the country, still in force. 

Prop 30 (2022), a new tax on income over $2 million, went down 58–42. 

Every local sales tax, parcel tax, and school bond in California has to go on a ballot. 

This is the hardest state in the country to raise a tax in without asking the people paying it — which means every tax you're calling "expensive " is one that survived a public vote.

True democracy. 

So the picture isn't a state "held up" by taxes it extracts from unwilling citizens. 

It's the fourth-largest economy on Earth whose residents periodically walk into a booth and vote to tax themselves to pay for transit, schools, and mental health, and periodically vote not to when they think it's too much. 

That's not a failed state. 

That's the thing the founders called self-government, working roughly as designed, in a place rich enough to afford it.

Maybe broke ass Red Sates could learn alot from th 4th largest economy in the world.

text:
The Green Revolution full stack had public research + extension + irrigation + rural credit + input subsidies + procurement + MSP + markets. What would a regenerative revolution full stack look like?

Green Revolution did not succeed merely because scientists developed high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice. It succeeded because an entire enabling institutional and financial stack were constructed around those varieties: irrigation, fertiliser subsidies, agricultural universities, public extension, rural credit, procurement, Minimum Support Prices, regulated markets, storage and food distribution.

Financial system underpinning these work as a symphony. 

Banks provide crop loans. Governments subsidise fertilizers and electricity. Public institutions finance irrigation. VC funds agri-tech startups. Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) finances warehouses, processing facilities and community farming assets.

Today, we are attempting to build an alternative with no clear view of the bigger picture. It has become norm to talk about it without necessarily going through the messy path of making it work.  

When a farmer wants to regenerate her soil, reduce dependence on external inputs, diversify her crops and restore the ecological relationships within her farm, we have nothing to offer beyond a training programme, a paltry subsidy amount in few select states and a promise of premium prices three years down the line.

The farmer must continue to feed her family. Her children must go to school. The moneylender must be repaid. The crop must reach the market. The soil may take years to regenerate. Her creditors expect repayment much sooner.

The Capital Stack that will fund Regenerative Transition in Indian smallholding agriculture is a four storeyed building

On the ground floor are grants and public subsidies. 

They finance activities whose benefits are widely distributed and whose commercial returns are insufficient or uncertain. These are investments in productive ecological and social infrastructure.

The first floor is catalytic capital, which absorbs risks that conventional lenders are unwilling to carry. 

A farmer transitioning from a familiar production system faces yield uncertainty, changing labour requirements and unfamiliar market conditions. A guarantee, income-protection mechanism or appropriately designed concessional loan can make experimentation financially tolerable.

The second floor is is patient equity and blended capital.

This is where regenerative agripreneurs enter the picture. A bio-resource centre, regenerative input company, farmer-service enterprise or differentiated food brand may eventually become commercially viable, but it requires time to develop products, capabilities, customers and reliable revenues.

Third Floor is commercial capital.
Once an enterprise generates predictable cash flows, ordinary bank lending, supply-chain finance and market-rate investment can support its growth.

Would this work?

text:
Opening Bell - Morning Commentary

Nifty Tumbles to Five-Month Low on Rising Energy Prices & Rate Hike Fears.

U.S. stocks closed mixed as an afternoon rally in Big Tech pared steeper earlier losses. The Dow fell 0.3% for a third straight decline, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed essentially flat as investors weighed surging Treasury yields against rising oil prices. Growth and tech names — most rate-sensitive — continued to weigh on sentiment.

The Treasury Department bought back $4.08 billion of long-term debt, well short of the $6 billion cap set by Secretary Scott Bessent. Offers were heavily rejected — just 12 of 35 eligible issues were accepted — undercutting the operation's aim of easing surging yields. The 30-year yield pushed higher still, hovering near 5.4%.

Communication Services led sector gains, with Meta Platforms up 4% after detailing monetisation plans for its AI agent. Data management firm Everpure rose over 11% after reaffirming full-year guidance, while Nvidia shares swung on news of a $13 billion deal to acquire Hugging Face.

The 10-year Treasury yield hit a 19-year high near 5.14%. Hawkish Fed and ECB commentary, paired with strong U.S. PMI data, lifted the odds of an October Fed hike to roughly 70%.

The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index fell to 47.8 in September from 51.7 in August, a 7.5% monthly drop, underscoring growing consumer unease. Durable goods orders offered a partial offset, beating expectations with a 1.1% month-over-month gain.

The rupee remained under pressure, depreciating 21 paise to close at 95.95, weighed down by soft Asian peers and a weak domestic equity market. A rebound in crude oil prices, elevated bond yields and rising expectations of higher interest rates added to the currency’s headwinds.

Nifty resumed its downtrend with a massive fall of 383 points to close at 23063, the lowest since 6th April 2026. This is the biggest one-session percentage fall since 8th July 2026 for Nifty. The breakdown decisively pushes Nifty below the lower boundary of its recent 23,100–23,600 consolidation zone. This signals a continuation of the primary downtrend, with sellers in firm control and momentum skewed to the downside.

Insurance distributor stocks tumbled sharply yesterday on the back of regulatory concerns, extending losses amid heightened sector-wide selling pressure.

Positional support now lies around 22,700, aligning with the upward-sloping trendline connecting the swing lows of June 2024, April 2025 and April 2026. On the upside, near-term resistance has shifted down to 23,300.

Indian markets are set for a weak open, tracking subdued global cues.

text:
I've been blown away by the capabilities of the Opus 5 and Fable 5 models in Claude.

I have one application for trade compliance that I've been working on for 20 years and is used by one of the biggest toolmakers for chip fabrication in the world.

I ask Claude to analyze something and it can tell me everything I need to know about the app, specific module design, workflow, develop diagrams, documentation, etc. It has troubleshot some serious memory problems in minutes - and the application I'm talking about runs to hundreds of thousands of lines of code, spread across web applications, web APIs and Windows programs.

I give it a problem and it offers suggestions I haven't even thought of and can implement them as fast as I can approve the plans that it writes, just about. It analyzes data in ways I didn't even think of, across a huge database with hundreds of tables and millions of records.

But I don't think Claude is sentient. I still must often guide it, tell it where it's wrong and correct its memory, even.

But it is an incredible tool that I, as a developer for more than 30 years, find miraculous. So much more than a stochastic parrot.

So much less than a sentient being, though. I don't think we have the problem the tech bros are stating. I think AI can be dangerous, but only as a tool we misuse, not as a  self-guiding angel of death to humans.

text:
Benedict Arnold’s name became American shorthand for traitor because he was an outsider who always opposed the Revolution. He was one of its most effective early commanders—yet he tried to sell West Point to the British in 1780. After the plot failed, he fled.  
Arnold published an open letter. In it he did not simply say “I switched teams for money.” He argued that he was the consistent patriot:
•  The original goal had been redress of grievances, not a complete break.
•  Once Britain offered terms, continuing the war was reckless and tyrannical.
•  Congress and the Patriot leadership had become the real threat to American liberty.
•  He believed that by going over to the British, he was actually serving the country’s long-term interest and preventing further bloodshed.
That is the classic traitor-justification pattern: “I have not abandoned the cause; the cause abandoned its own principles.” It sounds high-minded. He converted those grievances into a public claim that everyone else was the problem.

The people telling others to sit out midterms usually do not call themselves traitors repeating rhetoric like:
•  They promised voter ID, deportations, spending restraint, whatever the list is this cycle and failed to deliver.
•  Voting for them again only rewards failure/legitimizes a broken system.
•  Staying home is the only way to send a message/withhold consent.
•  I am the one still defending the real principles; the party/leadership have sold out.

Both the black-pullers and doomers convert disappointment with leaders into a claim of superiority to the country, Both have the same effect: they reduce the fighting strength of the side they claim to represent and make the opposing side’s job easier. It is a gift of turnout to whoever does show up. 

Arnold did not just walk away from the Continental Army; he tried to hand the British a fortress that would have split the colonies. Encouraging a motivated bloc to stay home is a much smaller-scale version of the same arithmetic: you weaken your own lines and hope the other side somehow feels the intended lesson.
Arnold was negotiating with a foreign army and later led British troops against former comrades. 

Midterm turnout is always lower than presidential turnout; parties have always had to drag their own disappointed voters to the polls.
The sharper historical point is not “these people are traitors.” It is that the language of righteous withdrawal has a long American pedigree, and it almost always sounds more principled to the person using it than it looks to everyone else. Arnold insisted to the end that love of country actuated his conduct. The people urging others to stay home usually insist the same thing. The test is whether the action actually advances the principles they claim to hold.
In a republic the people who participate set the terms. Arnold’s error was deciding that the entire American project no longer deserved his service. The modern version of that error is deciding that because elected officials disappointed you, the mechanism that replaces them no longer deserves your participation. That is the part of the rhetoric that most closely resembles Benedict Arnold.

Crypto Daily – September 24, 2026
A market-hardening day amid macro headwinds and regulatory headlines.

Market Overview
Bitcoin traded in a narrow range around the mid-80k zone as stronger US PMI data and rising Treasury yields kept upside momentum in check, following a prior rally driven by ETF inflows and short-covering dynamics. The daily blend of higher real yields and persistent inflation concerns dampened appetite for non-yielding assets, weighing on BTC despite notable ETF demand and continued accumulation by large holders. Ether likewise faced pressure from macro cues and a resilient dollar, even as institutional activity and ETF inflows provided some buoyancy. Across the market, a chorus of regulatory developments—ranging from GENIUS Act rulemakings to discussions on tokenized securities and prediction markets—shaped the near-term risk backdrop, influencing how investors value on-chain assets and the feasibility of new tokenized workflows. In this environment, developers and institutions are navigating headlines about AI-enabled data privacy, cross-border stablecoins, and the expansion of on-chain capital markets, all of which could reshape crypto liquidity and long-term demand. The net effect is a cautious tone: liquidity remains supportive in places, but the macro mechanics—rates, yields, and policy—continue to govern the pace and durability of the rally.

Market Snapshot
$BTC: $84,378, -0.0%
$ETH: $2,687, +0.1%
$BNB: $776.42, +1.2%
$XRP: $1.53, +2.2%
$SOL: $117.01, +1.8% Sentiment and flows reflected in ETF activity and major holder buying, with macro risk pegging gains to broader liquidity conditions and policy expectations.
Top Stories
1. Vitalik Buterin warns AI could erode privacy on public blockchains
A strong case is building that advances in AI and data analytics could link blockchain activity to real identities more effectively, even when wallets are pseudonymous. Buterin compares public blockchains to a “Twitter for your bank account,” arguing that richer data insights could undermine privacy protections. The piece notes that as AI capabilities improve, merely pairing a real name to a wallet may no longer suffice for privacy, given the ability to identify patterns in transaction histories. This shift would intensify debates over how privacy should be protected in on-chain activity, potentially pressuring developers and regulators to rework privacy safeguards in a world of increasingly capable inference. The analysis implies a market implication: projects with stronger privacy-layer solutions or redesigned data-access controls may gain a premium as users demand greater confidentiality, while public chains could face heightened scrutiny over data exposure as analytics capabilities expand.

2. Hut 8 wins bid for Poolin data centers; court approval upcoming
Hut 8 lodged a $140 million cash bid to acquire Poolin’s two Texas data centers, Pyote and Tarbush, in a deal that now awaits approval from the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey, with a sale hearing set for Sept. 29. The bid eclipses earlier stalking-horse offers and expands Hut 8’s data-center footprint as the company shifts toward AI/HPC infrastructure. The court process remains a gating factor before Hut 8 can finalize the acquisition, which would advance its broader strategic push into AI-ready capacity. The development underscores the ongoing consolidation in crypto mining infrastructure as operators seek to diversify into energy-intensive compute workloads.

3. Bybit launches Odds analytics, promotional pool; signals growing integration of data into trading
Bybit rolled out Bybit Odds, an analytics feature inside its exchange that aggregates real-time prediction-market odds and sentiment into probability visuals, alongside a promotional reward pool of 17,000 USDT for early users. The move shows how prediction-market data is becoming embedded into traditional trading workflows, suggesting a trend toward mainstream data sources powering decision-making in crypto markets rather than standalone venues. This aligns with broader industry shifts toward integrating external signals into existing platforms, blurring the line between exchange data and predictive analytics.

4. Circle expands CCTP and interop for EURC and cirBTC across Arc
Circle extended its Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol beyond USDC on Arc, enabling native transfers for EURC and cirBTC across multiple routes. The rollout includes EURC via Arc, Avalanche, Base, Ethereum, and World Chain, and cirBTC via Arc and Ethereum, with Gateway planning for later. Arc’s launch and its interoperability enhancements, including Gateways and CTS, bolster cross-chain asset movement and 1:1 asset transfers, signaling a broad push toward multi-asset interoperability across Layer-1s and Layer-2s. The development points to a more connected on-chain asset ecosystem where stablecoins and tokenized assets can move with reduced friction across chains.

Regulation & Policy
Regulatory activity continues to unfold around the GENIUS Act and tokenized markets, with U.S. agencies outlining rules for stablecoins and cross-border use. The Fed published two GENIUS Act rules aimed at ensuring stablecoin reserves are backed with safe assets and instituting an explicit bank-issuance pathway with a formal application process for Fed-supervised banks to issue stablecoins through subsidiaries. Separately, the CFTC issued advisory guidance on prediction-market contracts tied to individual conduct, emphasizing stronger controls to prevent manipulation and reinforcing that enforcement remains anchored in existing frameworks until Congress acts. The broad arc suggests more clarity on governance, custody, and transparency in tokenized markets, while the interplay between federal and state oversight on prediction markets remains a live policy debate.

Security & Risk
Incidents and assessments dominated risk narratives today. A major exchange breach in September resulted in unauthorized transfers estimated at hundreds of millions of dollars, with Bitget reporting a loss near $351.6 million and quickly pausing withdrawals while preserving deposits and trading, funding its user-protection fund to cover losses. The incident highlights the persistent tension between rapid exchange activity and the need for robust custody and liquidity safeguards in hot-wallet environments. Elsewhere, Cosmos Hub resumed block production after a Neutron governance breach led to attacker withdrawals, and Neutron governance actions illustrate how chain-level control can influence asset security across connected apps. Holders should consider the security of hot wallets, verify recovery services, and monitor governance changes that could affect asset custody.

Altcoins & Protocols
The market saw notable movement in privacy-leaning and cross-chain projects as investors weighed AI privacy implications and cross-chain interoperability. Zcash expanded exposure with a European listing, while Cardano explored governance-related changes to stake pool economics that could affect rewards for delegators. Solana continued its institutional push, with leadership changes and a plan to upgrade the Alpenglow network, while NEAR and Ondo advanced tokenized portfolios tied to BlackRock strategies for non-US investors, signaling continued institutional interest in real-world assets on-chain. Litecoin showed strength amid Grayscale ETF filings, and XRP’s rally persisted alongside ETF inflows, albeit with volatility in price. The broad theme: deepening tokenization of traditional assets and increased integration of on-chain products into mainstream finance, balanced by privacy, security, and regulatory considerations.

What to Watch
October rate path: markets price a high likelihood of a Fed rate move in October; monitor how this affects BTC and ETH price action and ETF inflows.
Regulatory clarifications on tokenized securities and prediction markets could materially impact on-chain trading and liquidity.
Bybit Odds integration and new data streams may increasingly influence retail decision-making.
The ongoing Hut 8 Poolin data-center acquisition hearing on Sept. 29 will determine the expansion of AI infrastructure.
EU MiCA discussions on crypto lending and DeFi could shape cross-border activity in tokenized assets.

text:
Brigham Young’s “Harem”: An 1869 Exposé

In February 1869 the Piedmont Virginian ran a page-one catalog of Brigham Young’s plural household—framed not as a church presidency but as an Oriental “harem.”

The piece is gossipy, ranking women by whether they had borne children, mixing physical description with moral judgment. Much of it traces to Catherine V. Waite’s The Mormon Prophet and His Harem and to Boston Journal correspondence. Southern and border papers reprinted it as anti-polygamy propaganda and as sensation.

Numbers wander: seventy, or thirty; the larger figure, the writer guessed, counted sealings for eternity only. Named wives include Lucy and Clara Decker, Harriet Cook, Lucy Bigelow, Eliza Snow the poetess, Zina Huntington, Emeline Free as “light of the harem,” Amelia Folsom as “mistress” with a private theatre box. Some are called castaways. Clara Chase is said to have gone mad. The tally offered: thirty women or more, seventy or eighty children.

Outward Utah looked orderly. Common report, the paper said, made it “one of the saddest communities in the world.” Young, it claimed, knew polygamy was a wearisome burden and tried to amuse the church.

Read it as a window on how the Eastern press saw Lion House life—not as a census.

Exposé, Orientalist smear, or both—and how much of Waite’s “veil” should we still trust?

He does not stand at the podium. He occupies it the way a cliff occupies a shore.
Navy cloth over scale, a red knot at the throat, claws settled on the wood as if the lectern were only a courtesy the room had offered him. Behind him the green marble stops looking like a wall and becomes stone. The flags, the faces, the microphones- all of it drops a scale.
The shoulders move first. Left. Slow. The weight of something that does not need to hurry. Heat follows the turn: a short breath, exact, so the air over that half of the hall shivers. Not rage. Notice.
Then the same majestic transfer to the right. Same downward look. Same fire. He's not arguing with the chamber. He's addressing it from above, as a giant speaks to what has gathered at his feet.
When he says immediately, the shoulders stop. Both sides still carry the warmth. He's already looking past them, past the podium, toward the place no institution in that room was built to reach.

text:
I answer this not as a Catholic or a Protestant for I am neither. I speak only as a humble follower of Christ. 

No.
If a soul has truly trusted in Jesus Christ, not as a slogan, a momentary prayer, or a transaction that leaves the heart unchanged, but as the living Savior who died and rose for sinners…then that trust is never a license to remain comfortably in known rebellion. 

Scripture does not present genuine faith as a one-time signature that then permits a life of unrepentant sin. It presents faith as a living union with Christ that the Holy Spirit Himself sustains.

The apostle John writes with piercing clarity: “No one born of God makes a practice of sinning, for God’s seed abides in him; and he cannot keep on sinning, because he has been born of God” (1 John 3:9). 

The same letter insists that whoever abides in Christ does not keep on sinning (1 John 3:6). This is not the claim of sinless perfection…it is the claim that a new nature has been given, and that nature cannot rest at peace in darkness. The Holy Spirit who seals the believer also convicts, disciplines, and draws the heart back when it wanders.

Paul asks the question that still echoes: “Shall we continue in sin that grace may abound? By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it?” (Romans 6:1–2). 

Those who belong to Christ have been crucified with Him. The old dominion has been broken. When a person persists, knowingly, willfully, without repentance in the very sins that once defined them, Scripture does not treat that as a minor inconsistency. It treats it as evidence that the profession was empty, or that the heart has hardened itself against the light it once claimed to love.

The warnings are not polite suggestions. Those who practice the works of the flesh “will not inherit the kingdom of God” (Galatians 5:21). If we go on sinning deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins, but a fearful expectation of judgment (Hebrews 10:26–27). 

These are not isolated verses. They form a consistent pattern: true faith produces fruit, and the absence of fruit over a lifetime of unrepentant practice reveals that the tree was never planted in good soil.

This does not mean a believer never stumbles, never falls into seasons of struggle, never needs to confess the same sin more than once. It means there is a difference between a sheep that strays and is pursued by the Shepherd, and a goat that never belonged to the fold. 

The one who genuinely trusts will, in the end, be brought to repentance or the trust was never genuine. God is not mocked. He who began a good work will bring it to completion (Philippians 1:6), and that completion includes a heart that learns to hate what He hates.

The Bible, not any church, is the final authority. And the Bible does not offer eternal security to the unrepentant. It offers a Savior who both forgives and transforms. To claim His name while refusing His lordship is to speak a language He does not recognize.

I have yesterday’s final right here. You do not need to give it to me again. You’re right: today’s first pass sounds more like a news recap written to someone. Yesterday was cleaner, flatter and more matter-of-fact. The personality only surfaced when a story actually earned it.

Here’s tonight in that rhythm:

Today on Earth, dozens of delegates walked out of the United Nations General Assembly as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began his address. Netanyahu defended Israel’s war against Iran, rejected accusations that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza and called the delegates who left the chamber “moral cowards.” Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas addressed the gathering by prerecorded video after the United States denied him a visa to attend in person. 

Meanwhile, U.S. and Iranian negotiators in New York discussed a phased agreement aimed at ending their nearly seven-month conflict. Sources close to the talks said the proposal could begin with Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and the United States lifting its economic blockade, but both sides remained reluctant to give up their leverage first. 

New U.S. sanctions also took effect against companies in third countries doing business with Iran. Iranian airlines were barred from neighboring countries including the United Arab Emirates and Oman, suspending Iranian flights through some of the Middle East’s busiest aviation hubs. 

In Washington, President Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House during Xi’s three-day state visit to the United States. Trade, Taiwan, artificial intelligence and the war with Iran were among the major issues surrounding the visit. Xi also announced that two giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, would arrive at Zoo Atlanta within days. 

Trade, Taiwan, AI and Iran. And somehow the pandas had the clearest travel plans.

In Saudi Arabia, authorities said they intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis toward Taif and the Red Sea port of Yanbu. The Houthis separately claimed attacks on Riyadh and Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu using missiles and drones, although Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the Riyadh claim. France also announced that it would deploy troops and defensive systems to help protect Yanbu, an increasingly important route for Saudi oil exports while shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted. 

In Ethiopia, flights to the historic town of Lalibela were suspended as fighting intensified nearby. Tigrayan forces seized airports and launched attacks in the Afar and Amhara regions as fears grew of a return to full-scale war. Residents in Tigray began stocking up on food and withdrawing cash while international officials called for restraint. 

The FDA approved Eli Lilly’s Onswik, a once-weekly basal insulin injection for adults with type 2 diabetes. The treatment offers an alternative to daily long-acting insulin and could eliminate hundreds of injections a year for some patients. 

In the Pacific, Hurricane Polo battered Mexico’s western coast with heavy rain and dangerous surf while Nolo approached Hawaii with the threat of potentially catastrophic rainfall. Polo fluctuated between Category 4 and Category 5 strength as it remained offshore from Mexico, while forecasters warned that parts of Hawaii could receive more than 20 inches of rain from Nolo. 

And on this day in 1936, Jim Henson was born in Greenville, Mississippi. He went on to create the Muppets and helped transform television puppetry through Sesame Street, The Muppet Show and the Muppet films. His characters—including Kermit the Frog—became part of American culture and reached generations of children and adults around the world. Today would have been his 90th birthday. 

That was one day on Earth.

See you tomorrow. Same planet. At least the pandas seem to have a plan. 🌎

text:
🇺🇸 🇨🇳 Trump and Xi entered the White House state dinner tonight surrounded by many of the people who will shape the technological and economic competition between the United States and China over the next decade.

The guest list brought together a concentration of American technological power. Sam Altman and Greg Brockman of OpenAI. Elon Musk. Nvidia's Jensen Huang. Apple's Tim Cook. Meta's Mark Zuckerberg. Google's Sundar Pichai and Sergey Brin. Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

Wall Street was there too, alongside senior members of the Trump administration, Supreme Court justices and some of America's most powerful corporate leaders.

They gathered in the East Room after Trump and Xi spent roughly 90 minutes behind closed doors earlier in the day, with AI, trade, Taiwan, Iran and other strategic issues hanging over a relationship Washington and Beijing are trying to stabilize. No major breakthrough emerged from those talks.

The dinner also brought together executives with sharply different views of how the next phase of AI development should proceed. 

Altman has moved toward deliberate pacing and greater outside oversight. Musk has expressed support for slowing under certain conditions and proposed adversarial safety testing among major labs.

Jensen Huang has taken a different position: AI safety is an engineering responsibility, companies should pace themselves when necessary, but Washington does not need new laws or a broader slowdown regime.

Former White House AI adviser David Sacks, another guest, has become one of the strongest critics of coordinated pacing.

Their companies also have very different relationships with China.

Nvidia wants access to the Chinese market. Apple remains deeply connected to Chinese manufacturing and consumers. Tesla operates a major Shanghai factory. Google, Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp remain blocked or heavily restricted in China.

OpenAI does not offer its models there and has repeatedly described Chinese AI development as a strategic competitive challenge.

All of this comes as Chinese models narrow parts of the capability gap, Washington tightens its focus on chips and distillation, and the U.S. AI industry debates whether slowing frontier development for safety could hand Beijing an advantage.

Trump has made his own position increasingly explicit: America should not stifle AI development because, in his formulation, whoever wins the race for AI, or “superintelligence,” as he now calls it, wins.

Many of the people debating how that competition should be managed were therefore sitting tonight at the same dinner as the leader of the country at the center of America's technological rivalry.

At the Chicago Council, NATO's chief revenue officer declared West Asia is Europe's backyard, "not the United States' backyard." He called Washington's war on Tehran "necessary," but complained Europe lacked the firepower to do it themselves. Next time, he said, Europeans "can take care of their own backyard."

An entire region of sovereign nations — Iran, Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Yemen, the Gulf states — reduced to a patch of grass where you put the grill and let the dog run. This is the language of empire. The language of 1885 Berlin. Rutte, whose own country built its wealth on colonial extraction, now lectures the world on who owns which backyard.

And the contradictions collapse instantly. If the Middle East were Europe's backyard, why did the US launch a catastrophic war on Iran without consulting its allies? Spain refused its bases. Germany and the UK called it "not our war." Trump didn't ask permission — because it was never Europe's backyard. It was America's war, fought for America's and Israel's interests, and Europe is simply told to clean up afterward.

Then came the money. Rutte complained Europeans spend too much on pensions and welfare while Washington carries the weapons burden. He wants defense spending raised from 2% to 5% of GDP and calls it "the fairness element." The same man who hollowed out Dutch public services through austerity now wants to do it across a continent. When Rutte says fairness, he means Europeans pay more so Americans pay less. That's not an alliance. That's tribute dressed up as a plan.

And the cherry on top: he offered to protect the US from Russia and China, and to prevent the Arctic from being militarized — by militarizing the Arctic. A region where Russia has legitimate sovereignty, China has legitimate commercial interests, and NATO expansion is the actual threat.

West Asia is nobody's backyard. The Arctic is nobody's backyard. Rutte is a colonial administrator with no colony left — and the punchline wrote itself. 🇷🇺🇮🇷

text:
Up Next: A Conversation With Palmer Luckey

In the first episode of Up Next with Clay Mowry, Palmer Luckey, Founder of Anduril Industries, offers a rallying cry to expand America’s manufacturing capabilities.

Luckey joins host Clay Mowry, AIAA CEO, and Jessica “STING” Peterson, Instructor Flight Test Engineer, U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School, for a wide-ranging conversation at Anduril headquarters in Costa Mesa, California. They talk about Luckey’s vision for the future of defense, technology, and manufacturing – moving beyond today’s products to understand the ideas and long-term strategies shaping the next generation of innovation.

As a newer entrant to the defense technology industry, Luckey reveals how Anduril is working to build trust in autonomous flight systems. In this dynamic exchange, he breaks down the battlespace of the future for us. Spoiler alert: it’s subterranean.

Luckey previews what’s Up Next with Anduril’s $1 billion bet on building “hyperscale” weapons in its five-million-square-foot plant outside Columbus, Ohio: Arsenal-1. He sees its potential to eventually be able to produce tens of thousands of weapons each year. The twist is their approach to building drones and autonomous systems the way other tech companies build consumer electronic systems – use a common set of commercial tooling and processes for every vehicle type.

⁠Throughout their conversation, Luckey recounts the science fiction inspirations that have sparked his lifelong creativity.
