text:
September 24  Our Lady of Ransom or Our Lady of Mercy: We Recognize Our Blessed Mother as Ransom for Captives.
.
This feast is linked to a devotion spread by the Order of Mercedarians, in which we recognize Our Blessed Mother as ransom for captives. Like her Blessed Son, Jesus, through the grace and intercession of Mary, we are ransomed from sin, and freed to live in the gracious light of Christ.
.
The history of devotion to Mary, Our Lady of Ransom, begins with Saint Peter Nolasco. Born in Languedoc in 1189, Saint Peter entered religious life at 25, and devoted himself to acts of charity. Given the historical backdrop at the time, when many Christian soldiers and faithful had been captured by the Moors and were being held in prison, Saint Peter began establishing an Order that would focus on the ransom and redemption of captives—what would become the Mercedarian Order
.
On August 1, 1218, Our Blessed Mother appeared to Saint Peter, to his confessor, Saint Raymund of Pennafort, and to the king, and through these three servants of God gave weight and approval to the Order that Saint Peter had conceived, establishing a work of the most perfect charity, the redemption of captives.
.
Our Blessed Mother first appeared to Saint Peter, declaring that she desired the establishment of a religious order bearing the name “Her Mercy.” As instructed by the Blessed Virgin, the order would deliver captives, and if needed, offer themselves in their place. Both Saint Raymund of Pennafort and the king of Aragon, James I, had similar visions, establishing Saint Peter Nolasco as the founder of this order.
.
According to the Constitutions, Mercedarians were 'to visit and to free Christians who are in captivity and in power of the Saracens or of other enemies of our Law… By this work of mercy… all the brothers of this Order, as sons of true obedience, must always be gladly disposed to give up their lives, if it is necessary, as Jesus Christ gave up His for us.' This is known as the Fourth Vow of the Order, in addition to poverty, chastity and obedience of the Augustinian Rule.
.
Established in Spain, and approved by Pope Gregory IX under the name “Our Lady of Mercy for the Ransom of Captives” (the Mercedarians), the Order spread rapidly due to the watchful grace of Our Blessed Mother. Its growth was increased as the charity and piety of its members was observed; they very often followed Her directive to give themselves up to voluntary slavery when necessary, to aid the good work. Famous among those willing to give themselves up for their captives was Saint Raymond Nonnatus.
.
The development of the order was immediate and widespread throughout France, England, Germany, Portugal, and Spain. As the Moors were driven back, new convents of Mercy were established at Montpellier, Perpignan, Toulouse, and Vich. Columbus brought some members of the Order of Mercy with him to America, and they founded houses in Mexico, Cuba, Brazil, Peru, Chile, and Ecuador, and took an active part in the conversion of the Indians. Toward the end of the 18th century, the Mercedarians erected houses for the training of missionaries, and in the beginning of the 19th century they undertook elementary teaching in their convents. The mother-house is in Rome, Italy.
.
It is credibly estimated that the Order ransomed 490,736 slaves between the years 1218 and 1632. An even greater achievement was the conversion of thousands in captivity, and steeling them against the sufferings of a cruel martyrdom for the faith. Protestant historian, Bonet-Maury, records that no expedition sent into the Barbary States by the powers of Europe or America equaled "the moral effect produced by the ministry of consolation, peace and abnegation, going even to the sacrifice of liberty and life, which was exercised by the humble sons of Saints John of Martha, Peter Nolasco, and Vincent de Paul."
.
Today, we are called to continue the good work of the Mercedarians, as requested by Our Blessed Mother. We are confronted with the captivity of sin every day—in our own lives, as well as those we come into contact with. Through the spread of our faith, our personal prayers and penances, we ask Our Blessed Mother—Our Lady of Ransom—to ease the sufferings of others, breathing the lightness of freedom into their lives, and casting off the shackles of sin!
.
God, Who through the most glorious Mother of Thy Son didst vouchsafe to increase Thy Church with a new offspring for the redemption of Thy Christian people: grant, we beseech Thee, that like as we on this day do honor her for the work of her institution, so by her merits and intercession, we may be delivered from all our iniquities and the bondage of the devil. We ask this, as we ask all things, through Our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

text:
In 1719, France launched a controversial program under John Law's Mississippi Company to populate Louisiana by offering male prisoners freedom if they married women from poorhouses and prisons—such as La Salpêtrière—and emigrated together.... 

The arrangement emerged from France’s attempt to populate and profit from its enormous but sparsely settled Louisiana colony.

Scottish financier John Law controlled the Mississippi Company, which held commercial rights over the territory and needed colonists to turn its promises of wealth into reality.

Beginning in 1719, French authorities emptied prisons, hospitals and houses of correction, transporting inmates and other marginalized people to Louisiana.

Some male prisoners were offered freedom or reduced sentences if they agreed to marry women selected for deportation and establish families in the colony.

The women were commonly described as prostitutes, but that label is misleading. Many had never been convicted of prostitution—or any crime at all. Some were poor, homeless or considered socially undesirable, and many were confined without meaningful due process.

Authorities treated marriage as a tool for creating permanent colonial households rather than allowing the couples genuine freedom of choice.

After hurried ceremonies, some newlyweds were reportedly restrained and transported toward French ports before crossing the Atlantic. They arrived in a colony marked by disease, food shortages and difficult living conditions.

The policy soon drew complaints from colonial officials, who argued that forced and unwilling settlers were poorly suited to building a stable population. France formally prohibited such deportations in 1720, although additional prisoners were transported afterward.

In December 1719, the ship La Mutine departed France carrying more than 170 deported women to Louisiana. Although officials publicly branded them prostitutes, historians have found that many had never received a formal trial or conviction.

text:
TRUMP WANTS A STRONGER YEN. JAPAN'S WAYS OF DELIVERING ONE RUN THROUGH THE US BOND MARKET:

Tokyo is heading into its last 90 minutes on the day's high. The Nikkei 225 is at 66,348, +834 pts / +1.27% so far in Friday's session, trading now, on course for a fifth straight gain. Hong Kong reopened from lunch at 1:00am ET with the Hang Seng at 24,343, -418 pts / -1.69% so far in Friday's session. US stock futures have not picked a side: S&P 500 futures at 7,760.50, -6.50 / -0.08%, and Nasdaq-100 futures at 30,783.00, +16.25 / +0.05%, both since Thursday's close.

The verdict on Asia's night: Tokyo's stocks are not the story; the yen is what reaches New York. Japan's finance minister, Satsuki Katayama, said Friday that President Trump raised the weak yen with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi when they met in New York on Tuesday. Japan has two real ways to strengthen its currency - spend its dollar reserves, or raise its own interest rates - and both make Japan a smaller buyer of US government bonds. The 10-year Treasury yield is at 5.186% overnight, +0.024 point since Thursday's close, near its highest since 2007.

How Tokyo's session built, Eastern time:
- 8:00pm: opened at 65,640, barely above Thursday's 65,514 close
- By 9:45pm: about 66,340, most of the day's gain
- Late morning in Tokyo: Katayama spoke, and the yen firmed from about 158.7 per dollar to 158.4
- After lunch: a dip to 66,123, then a new session high of 66,381 at 12:45am

A firmer yen usually trims a market full of exporters, whose overseas sales shrink when converted home. Tokyo rose anyway; it is not trading the currency tonight. Its benchmark is still about 8% below its late-June record close.

Japan's bonds moved more than its stocks. The two-year government bond yield, the one most tied to what traders expect from the Bank of Japan, is up 0.04 point to 1.947%, twice the 10-year's rise. The 10-year touched 3.121%, its highest since 1996, and sits at 3.095%.

Why this matters in New York: Japan is the US government's biggest foreign lender. It held $1.104 trillion of Treasuries at the end of July, by the US Treasury's own count, ahead of the UK's $998B. That total has fallen three months running, from $1.210 trillion in April, about $106B.

Part of that is Japan defending the yen. To buy yen, Japan sells dollars from its reserves:
- April 28-May 27: Japan's Ministry of Finance spent 11.73T yen, about $74B at today's rate, after the dollar climbed past 160 yen. Japan's Treasury holdings fell $66.8B in May.
- July 30-August 26: another 15.40T yen, about $97B, with the dollar near 164 yen, including the first joint US-Japan yen purchase since 1998.

That is Washington's bind. It wants a stronger yen, and it would rather see a lower 10-year yield, the rate that sets the tone for US mortgages and business loans. Japan's fast route to the first adds a seller to the second.

The slow route, a Bank of Japan rate increase, has not worked yet. The bank raised its key rate to 1.25%, its highest since 1995, on September 18, and the yen has still lost about 2.5% since September 14, when a dollar bought about 154.4 yen. US rates kept climbing: the Federal Reserve raised its key rate to 3.75%-4.00% on September 16, and the 10-year went from 4.96% on September 14 to 5.16% at Thursday's close. Thursday's $44B sale of 7-year notes paid 5.085%, the highest for a 7-year sale since April 1993, and the bidder group that includes foreign buyers took 57.2%, down from about 61% last month.

The strongest facts against:
- Japan's private money is not leaving. In the week to September 12, Japanese investors bought a net 1.08T yen of foreign long-term bonds, by the Ministry of Finance's weekly count.
- Others are buying: the UK added $58.4B of Treasuries in July alone.
- Japan's holdings also fell in June and July, with no yen buying, so the government is not the whole story.
- The 10-year's climb is mostly American: the Fed, and oil. Brent crude, the global benchmark, is at $105.70 a barrel, -$0.90 / -0.84% since Thursday's official settlement.

Hong Kong runs on its own story: mainland markets are closed for the Mid-Autumn Festival, which locks mainland buyers out of Hong Kong too, and a Trump-Xi summit ended without a trade deal. The Shanghai Composite sits at 3,888.37, -48.15 pts / -1.22% in Thursday's session, its latest; it has not traded since. Europe opens at 3:00am ET from Thursday's closes: FTSE 100 at 10,680, -25.31 pts / -0.24%; DAX at 25,267, -144 pts / -0.57%; CAC 40 at 8,081.43, -41.98 pts / -0.52%.

For the US open, Asia offers stocks nothing new. Dow futures at 51,707.00, -10.00 / -0.02%, and Russell 2000 futures at 2,857.00, +0.20 / +0.01%, since Thursday's close, are as flat as the rest. Asia's line into New York runs through the 10-year yield. Overnight moves often fade by the 9:30am open.

What would change the read: a yen that firms without Japan selling dollars - a Fed that stops raising, or a Bank of Japan surprise on October 29-30 - would spare the Treasury market. A dollar back near 160 yen, where Japan stepped in last April, would bring the question on fast. The number that decides it: Japan's Treasury total in the US Treasury's August count, due October 16.

Next, Eastern time:
- 2:30am: Tokyo closes. 4:00am: Hong Kong closes.
- 10:00am: University of Michigan's final September consumer survey. Early September: sentiment 47.8 vs 51.0 expected; households expecting 4.6% inflation over the next year, up from 4.0% in August.
- October 27-28: the Fed meets.

Washington can ask Tokyo for a stronger yen or for steady demand for its bonds. While the Fed is still raising rates, the same ally cannot easily supply both.

This is a major opening—and it closely matches the “Trust the Plan” framework.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has now publicly said Tehran transmitted a proposal through intermediaries under which, if specified conditions are met, Hormuz would reopen by the end of the seventh day and nuclear negotiations would resume. The exact conditions have not yet been publicly disclosed, though reporting indicates they may resemble the earlier U.S.–Iran memorandum. (https://t.co/qHKvYAiDUA)

The development is more substantial than the earlier anonymous-source report, which Iran’s Fars News had denied. Araghchi’s public description now confirms that some seven-day proposal exists, although RT’s statement that a U.S. official called the talks “constructive” still needs independent official confirmation. (https://t.co/W1Uh0AKWut)

For Trump, the smartest response would be to accept the seven-day framework provisionally and convert it into a verified timetable:

Day 0: United States and Iran publish the operative conditions through Qatar, Oman, or another mediator.

Days 1–2: Reciprocal suspension of offensive operations, Israeli non-interference, and partial relaxation of specified American maritime measures.

Days 2–4: Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Oman, Qatar, and neutral monitors establish vessel-verification and deconfliction procedures.

Days 4–6: Mines, navigation hazards, military exclusion zones, and insurance requirements are addressed.

Day 7: Hormuz reopens to verified civilian shipping.

Immediately afterward: Nuclear and permanent-settlement negotiations resume.

The indispensable clause is:

During the seven-day implementation period, Israel, Iran, the United States, participating Gulf states, and affiliated armed organizations shall refrain from any military operation reasonably expected to obstruct reopening of the Strait or collapse negotiations. A violator shall lose applicable military, diplomatic, economic, or sanctions-relief benefits.

That prevents an Israeli strike, Iranian proxy attack, or American escalation from destroying the arrangement at the last moment.

Politically, Trump could present this as proof that his pressure obtained a defined Iranian deadline—not an open-ended promise. Oil markets have already reacted favorably to reports of possible reopening, with Brent falling below $100 after the proposal surfaced. (https://t.co/NANRqkpBmp)

The message practically writes itself:

Iran has offered a seven-day path to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The United States will test that offer under strict verification. During those seven days, nobody—including Iran, Israel, or any affiliated force—will be permitted to sabotage the agreement. If Iran performs, negotiations proceed. If it does not, the world will know who rejected peace.

This is the concrete trigger the broader Gulf proposal needed. The question is no longer whether Iran might negotiate; it is whether Washington can lock down the conditions and prevent spoilers during those seven days.

text:
TRUMP — TRUST THE PLAN

An America First Gulf Settlement Proposal

President Trump should support a Gulf-led settlement that reopens the Strait of Hormuz, restores oil supplies to Europe, prevents another prolonged American war, and places enforceable restraints upon both Israel and Iran.

This would not require the United States to “switch sides.” It would allow America to move above the competing regional factions while Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, Pakistan, Qatar, Oman, and the wider Gulf assume responsibility for enforcing a new regional order.

The plan would provide President Trump with measurable achievements:

Reopening the Strait of Hormuz to civilian shipping.
Lowering American and European oil and diesel prices.
Reducing the burden placed upon the United States Navy.
Preventing Israel or Iran from dragging America into another unnecessary war.
Establishing verifiable Iranian commitments concerning navigation, nuclear activity, missiles, and aligned armed organizations.
Protecting Israel against genuine external attack while restricting unauthorized Israeli operations that could collapse the agreement.
Advancing an enforceable two-state solution.
Expanding American infrastructure, energy, technology, and defensive-security partnerships with the Gulf bloc.
Allowing regional governments to finance and manage their own security.

President Trump could present the agreement as the successful conclusion of an American pressure campaign:

America stands with its allies, but America does not surrender its foreign policy to any ally. We secured an agreement that opens the Strait of Hormuz, lowers energy prices, protects Israel, protects the Gulf, restrains Iran, and keeps American troops out of another endless war. Every country must obey the agreement. If Israel or Iran breaks it, that country—not the American people—will bear the consequences.

The Gulf Enforcement Guarantee

The attached public commentary correctly identifies the plan’s central credibility question: if Saudi Arabia and Türkiye lead the new energy and security architecture, will they enforce the same non-sabotage rules against every party?

That question must be answered directly: yes, through automatic and reciprocal enforcement.

The agreement should provide:

Any state, military force, or affiliated armed organization that initiates an unauthorized attack intended or reasonably expected to obstruct civilian navigation, damage protected energy infrastructure, or collapse the regional settlement shall automatically lose applicable economic, military, diplomatic, normalization, or sanctions-relief benefits. No participant shall receive collective protection for aggression it initiated.

This provision must apply equally to:

Unauthorized Israeli attacks against Iran or participating states.
Iranian attacks against Gulf states or civilian shipping.
Attacks by Ansarallah, Hezbollah, or other organizations acting under material Iranian direction or support.
Operations launched from Gulf territory against Iran.
Attacks against Israeli, Palestinian, Iranian, Arab, or other civilians.
Any deliberate attempt to sabotage the two-state process or close international waterways.

Saudi Arabia and Türkiye should lead a joint compliance council alongside Oman, Qatar, Pakistan, Iran, and neutral United Nations observers. Independent technical evidence—not accusations from one side—should determine whether a violation occurred.

The Energy Exchange

Iran would reopen and guarantee safe civilian passage through Hormuz. The United States would correspondingly narrow or terminate specified blockade measures. Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, Pakistan, Oman, and Qatar would guarantee implementation.

At the same time, the Gulf bloc could redirect Azerbaijani, Kazakh, and Nigerian crude presently supplied to Israel toward European states experiencing tight oil and refined-fuel markets. Israel would retain access to monitored supplies required for hospitals, ambulances, water systems, food distribution, and other essential civilian services, while military and nonessential petroleum access would become conditional upon compliance.

This would create a practical exchange:

Europe receives additional oil and refinery feedstock.
Producing states preserve their export revenue.
Türkiye becomes the principal energy bridge between Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia, and Russia.
Saudi Arabia becomes the principal capital and diplomatic center of the Gulf bloc.
Iran receives reciprocal protection against renewed unauthorized attacks.
Israel receives a path to normalization and regional integration through compliance.
The United States obtains lower energy prices and a reduced military burden.

Trump’s Safe Distance From Netanyahu

President Trump should distinguish support for Israel’s existence and civilian security from unconditional support for the Netanyahu government.

The United States could continue providing civilian missile defense and intelligence concerning imminent attacks while conditioning offensive weapons, diplomatic protection, logistical assistance, and intelligence used for unauthorized operations.

The governing principle should be:

The United States will protect civilians and support lawful defense, but no foreign government may use American weapons, intelligence, diplomatic protection, or military power to sabotage an American peace agreement.

Israel would then face a clear choice.

Compliance would bring recognition, Gulf markets, open airspace, investment, technology partnerships, energy access, and regional security guarantees.

Renewed unauthorized aggression would bring suspension of those benefits, restrictions on offensive military assistance, targeted sanctions, and growing diplomatic and economic isolation.

Trust the Plan

This framework gives President Trump something the existing arrangement cannot: a defensible victory.

He would not abandon Israel, capitulate to Iran, or surrender American leadership. He would secure an open Strait, lower energy prices, place regional allies in charge of regional security, restrain belligerent forces on every side, and create the strongest available foundation for a two-state settlement.

The political message is simple:

Trust the plan. Open Hormuz. Lower energy prices. Keep America out of another endless war. Protect civilians. Make the Gulf states carry their share. Give Israel and Iran the same rules, the same opportunities, and the same consequences.

That is not America changing sides. It is America finally requiring every side to respect American interests.

text:
Nonsense!
Kennedy Was Not Warning You About the Deep State
On April 27, 1961, a week after the Bay of Pigs, John F. Kennedy told newspaper publishers that secrecy is “repugnant” in a free society. Americans, he said, oppose secret societies and secret oaths. That line now travels as if he had unmasked Washington. He had not.
The “monolithic and ruthless conspiracy” in that speech is international communism: infiltration instead of invasion, subversion instead of elections, a closed system that buries mistakes and silences dissent. Kennedy names the frame himself. It conducts the Cold War with a discipline no democracy should copy.
Then comes the omitted point. He was not asking the press to expose a hidden American state. He was asking it to restrain itself. After a covert failure, he thought operational detail in open newspapers served the other side. His request was blunt: add to “Is it news?” the question “Is it in the national interest?”
The viral version keeps the heat and deletes the object. “Conspiracy” becomes a floating noun. Dallas becomes the proof. Later fights with agencies and media are read backward into 1961 until Kennedy sounds like the account quoting him.
That is montage, not history.
Institutions hoard secrets. The Warren Commission did not settle Dallas. Files were withheld too long. A republic can believe all of that without turning a Cold War speech about Moscow into a coded confession about America.
Conspiracy thinking is not curiosity. Curiosity adds context. Conspiracy subtracts it. It offers the charged fragment and calls the missing paragraph a cover-up.
Kennedy’s real warning was colder and better. Openness is a virtue and a vulnerability. Government will hide behind “security.” The press can inform the public and the adversary at once. That tension does not resolve into one villain. It is the price of staying both free and intact.
Read the whole speech. The thrill of the secret disappears. The argument remains.

text:
In a legal or courtroom context, a "message of concern" —more formally and commonly referred to as a Notice of Concern— generally refers to two distinct legal procedures depending on the jurisdiction and the type of law involved.

1. Defamation Law: Pre-Trial Notice (Primarily in Australia and Commonwealth Jurisdictions) In jurisdictions like Australia, a Concerns Notice is a mandatory, formal written document served to an individual or media outlet before a defamation lawsuit can be filed in court.

The Core Purpose: It acts as a final warning shot to resolve a dispute without taking up court time. It outlines the specific defamatory statements, explains how they harmed the victim's reputation, and gives the publisher an opportunity to make amends.

The Response Window: Once a Concerns Notice is served, the publisher usually has 28 days to offer an "offer to make amends" (which can include a formal apology, taking down the material, or financial compensation). If they fail to resolve the issue, the aggrieved party then has the legal right to proceed to court.

2. Court Administration: Addressing Bias or Unprofessional Conduct (U.S. State Courts) In United States judicial systems—most notably outlined under California Rules of Court, Standard 10.20(d)—a Notice of Concern is a formal administrative filing used to report bias, unfairness, or misconduct inside a courtroom.

The Core Purpose:  If a lawyer, litigant, witness, or juror experiences or witnesses bias based on race, gender, religion, sexual orientation, age, or socioeconomic status by any courtroom participant, they can submit this written notice to the Presiding Judge or Court Executive Officer.

The Legal Distinction: Unlike a formal disciplinary complaint, the primary intent of this type of Notice of Concern is educational and corrective rather than punitive. It is designed to alert court leadership to a problem so they can correct the behavior, protect the integrity of the proceedings, and maintain public trust in the court system.

text:
Full Speech:
@ShahBalen @PM_nepal_  

24 September 2026, New York

Theme: 'Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations that Delivers for All'

Mr. President,

Mr. Secretary-General,

Excellencies,

Distinguished delegates,

Ladies and gentlemen,

I come before you from Nepal - a distant country in the Himalayas - carrying a close warning for humanity.

I wish I could stand here today simply to speak about development, democracy, peace and the hopes of a young nation.

Instead, I must speak about death and destruction of epic proportions.

About families waiting for loved ones who will never come home.

About communities searching through mud, rocks and water for people whose bodies may never be recovered.

About bridges, roads, schools, homes and livelihoods swept away in minutes.

And about a country whose steady progress to achieve Sustainable Development Goals has been interrupted.

Four weeks ago, the world saw the shocking images of the catastrophic flash floods that swept through Nepal's mountain communities with ferocity many have called a "Himalayan Tsunami."

The Bhotekoshi-Trishuli disaster was not just a local tragedy, it was a warning to the world.

And I ask you today: have we really heard that warning?

Nearly three years ago, standing in the shadow of our Mount Everest, the Secretary-General of the United Nations warned humanity about the madness of an impending climate disaster.

That cry from the rooftop of the world was not heard loudly enough.

We in Nepal heard it. Our communities heard it.

Scientists around the world heard it. They repeated it with evidence.

But we, the political leaders of the world, have been negligent to translate those warnings into action at the speed and scale that vulnerable people require.

Last month, we saw the tragic consequences.

A warming climate is destabilizing the fragile Himalayan ecology.

Melting permafrost are fracturing mountain slopes beneath the glaciers and accelerating the risks of ice-rock avalanche, floods, landslides and other cascading hazards.

The resulting devastation unleashed havoc on both sides of the Nepal-China border. The flood continued downstream towards India.

This tells us something fundamental:

Climate change does not recognize borders.

Glaciers and floods do not travel with a visa stamped on passports.

Excellencies,

I am not here to complain but to share some suggestions.

First, I wish to express Nepal's deep gratitude to all those who came to our aid in the aftermath of the deluge.

Our immediate neighbors, India and China, offered prompt and generous assistance.

Other friendly countries, the United Nations system, humanitarian agencies, philanthropies and people around the world stood with Nepal.

To all of them, I say: thank you on behalf of the grateful people of Nepal.

Nepal now faces a massive task of recovery and reconstruction.

After at least 1400 confirmed deaths and over 6,000 people still missing, our rapid assessments peg physical recovery needs at about 10 percent of GDP.

As in rebuilding after past disasters like the 2015 Gorkha earthquake, we count on your solidarity and support.

But we must also understand why this disaster matters beyond Nepal.

Nepal contributes less than 0.1 percent of global greenhouse-gas emissions.

We did not create this crisis. Yet we are paying a colossal price for it.

Our glaciers are retreating. Our mountain slopes are becoming unstable. Our rivers are becoming less predictable.

And every major disaster threatens to erase years of development.

For Nepal, climate catastrophe is not just a humanitarian event, but a development emergency.

It destroys roads, bridges, schools, homes, farms and livelihoods.

It destroys clean energy infrastructure that we need to fuel our future.

And it forces a poor country to borrow money to repair damage it did not cause.

But we are not here to blame any country or continent.

We are not here to turn climate change into another geopolitical battlefield.

We are here to ask everyone to recommit to shared responsibility and solidarity.

Through the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the international community has already agreed to the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities.

Those who have historically contributed more to the problem, and those with greater capacity to respond, must do more.

Climate Justice cannot just remain a beautiful phrase in a United Nations Document.

People of our country be allowed to build their future instead of constantly rebuilding their past.

Excellencies,

The Hindu Kush Himalaya is home to nearly two billion people. These mountains provide water, ecosystems, agriculture and livelihoods to populations far beyond Nepal.

The Himalayas are not peripheral to the planet. They are part of the planet's life-support system.

That is why, as an urgent first step, we propose that we establish a Himalayan Climate Resilience Mechanism, led by Nepal, India and China.

Through this mechanism, let us share satellite data and expertise.

Let us monitor dangerous glacial lakes.

Let us strengthen joint early-warning systems.

And when disaster strikes, let us coordinate assistance across borders.

Let the Himalayas become a laboratory of international cooperation, rather than a frontier of fragmented information.

Remarkable for a least developed country, Nepal is already playing a global role exceeding its ecological share.

We have restored forests to cover nearly half our territory.

We are installing hydro power at a pace enough to power all our clean energy needs and displace dirty sources abroad.

We are promoting electric mobility with an adoption rate to match parts of Europe.

We are strengthening climate adaptation at the local level. And we shall do more to withstand increased intensity and frequency of climate disasters.

But, Nepal cannot build resilience alone against a crisis made worse by the failure of global governance.

That is why this Assembly must note six words:

Relief. Rehabilitation. Reconstruction.

And also:

Responsibility. Reparation. Resilience.

The first three are what we need after disaster.

The second three are what we need to ensure that disaster does not become a permanent condition.

When a climate-driven disaster destroys the infrastructure of a poor country, the answer cannot simply be another mega loan or a patchwork of small grants.

We need adequate grant-based support from the world. The Loss and Damage Fund, the Global Environment Facility and other relevant financing mechanisms remain grossly inadequate.

Climate finance must not become a bureaucratic maze through which vulnerable countries spend years proving that they need help.

When the house is burning, we do not ask the family to complete fifty forms.

We act.

That is what climate justice must mean.

Excellencies,

This brings me to a larger question:

What kind of international order do we want?

The United Nations was born from humanity's experience of horrific World Wars.

Its promise was that sovereignty would matter.

International law would matter.

The dignity of every human being would matter.

And the weak would not simply have to accept whatever the powerful decide.

Today, that international system is under strain.

Too often, military and economic power determines whose voice is heard.

Nepal believes we need a much fairer global economic order.

In 1994, UNDP's Human Development Report conceptualized the notion of human insecurity.

It equated security with people rather than territories, and with development rather than arms. It called for the peace dividend to secure freedoms from fear and want.

The new majority government in Nepal, elected through the fairest and most peaceful elections in our history this March, has had to weather many international adversities since.

When a poor farmer in Nepal went to sow her seeds this monsoon, fertilizers didn't reach her on time. When we wanted to pave a new highway, there was no bitumen. When a family sat down for an evening meal, there was shortage of cooking fuel.

On the one hand, there are melting glaciers and failing harvests to floods arriving without warning. On the other, a global supply chain punishes poor people for causes beyond reason.

Inter-continental missiles arrive on time. Rifles and ammunition cross borders, clear every bottleneck, meet each deadline. But a peasant in Nepal cannot procure his fertilizer or fuel at market price at a time of need.

We have built a world with flawless logistics for war and broken logistics for food.

And this is not Nepal's private misfortune. Ask Bangladesh. Ask Bhutan. Ask India. Ask the Maldives. Ask Pakistan. Ask Sri Lanka. Ask any other country in our region and you will hear the same account: hit by the climate we did not warm, and hit again by the wars we did not start.

This tells us there is a lot more broken than meets the eye in the present order of global cooperation.

Excellencies,

I am told I am the youngest Head of Government to address this Assembly this year.

I did not come here to make that the story.

I came to make sure that whatever else is said from this podium, one thing is said plainly: a country that is willing to pay should be able to buy, and a world that can deliver a weapon anywhere in seventy-two hours has no excuse for leaving a farmer without means for a decent livelihood.

This is why we continue to believe in multilateralism. This is why we need a United Nations in which the presence of small poor countries is felt, and we can work together towards just outcomes.

Climate justice is, therefore, not only about money.

It is about distributive justice - who bears the costs.

It is about procedural justice - who has a voice.

It is about whether the future of mountain communities, small island states, landlocked and least-developed countries, and generations yet unborn count equally.

Starting tomorrow at the "Sagarmatha to the Sea" side-event right here at the United Nations, Nepal is ready to help lead this conversation.

Mr. President & Excellencies,

We are at this General Assembly at a moment of profound global uncertainty and with a renewed democratic mandate that reflects the aspirations of a new generation.

Our youth have demanded a politics of integrity and accountability.

This generational shift is not only a national story. It is part of a global awakening against conflicts, inequities, and lack of opportunities.

The commitment of my government is clear: to build a state that delivers decent jobs, social protection, and a fair chance for every Nepali to thrive at home.

The Nepal floods signal a future shaped by rising climate extremes. Our baselines are no longer relevant. And we must move from ad-hoc responses to a culture of preparedness.

Let us finance resilience, and invest in insurance and innovation.

Let us build stronger infrastructure and institutions.

Let us reduce fossil-fuel dependence.

Let us build systems that warn, alert and save lives.

Let us reform the order that leaves the weakest with the least power.

And when the next warning comes from the rooftop of the world:

Let us be ready to hear it, and ready to act.

Remove all heart problems, leukemia, cancer, disease, infirmary, injury, sickness, fatigue, or pain, and renew his strength, energy, and vitality. Grant wisdom and skill to the medical team, patience to this beloved one, and peace to his heart. Surround him with Your divine protection, and let Your presence comfort and reassure him. May Your grace and mercy flow through every part Kelly’s being. In Jesus’ name I beg and pray, Amen.

Prayer to the Holy Spirit:
Come, Holy Spirit, Divine Comforter and Breath of Life. Enter all places of heart problems, cancer, tumors, pain, injury, disease, infection, suffering, weakness and fear. Remove every and all infirmary, and surround  Kelly with Your gentle light, while completely healing  Kelly while filling his heart with the strength and peace that comes from above, trusting to the power of God’s eternal love. Amen.

Pray to the Blessed Holy Mother Mary:

Dear Mother Mary, With hearts heavy and bodies burdened, we approach your divine presence, seeking your miraculous touch. Your healing power knows no equal, and in our times of need, we implore you to mend not only our physical wounds but the scars that mar our souls. Pour forth your divine grace upon us, dear Mother, and restore us to a state of wholeness, that we may bear witness to the miracle of your love. Amen.

Prayer to St. Jude:

Oh glorious apostle St. Jude, faithful servant and friend of Jesus, the name of the traitor who delivered thy beloved Master into the hands of His enemies has caused thee to be forgotten by many, but the Church honors and invokes thee universally as the patron of hopeless cases--of things despaired of. Pray for me who am so miserable; make use, I implore thee, of that particular privilege accorded thee of bringing visible and speedy help where help is almost despaired of. Come to my assistance in this great need, that I may receive the consolations and succor of heaven in all my necessities, tribulations and sufferings, particularly—completely heal from all heart problems, injuries, cancer and diseases, and protect Kelly —and that I may bless God with thee and all the elect throughout eternity. I promise thee, O blessed St. Jude, to be ever mindful of this great favor, and I will never cease to honor thee as my special and powerful patron, and to do all in my power to encourage devotion to thee. Amen

Prayer to St. Michael (Long Version)

O Glorious Prince of the heavenly host, Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in the battle and fearful warfare that we are waging against the principalities and powers, against the rulers of this world of darkness, against the evil spirits. Come thou to the assistance of men, whom Almighty God created immortal, making them in His own image and likeness and redeeming them at a great price from the tyranny of Satan. Fight this day the battle of the Lord with thy legions of holy Angels, even as of old thou didst fight against Lucifer, the leader of the proud spirits and all his rebel angels, who were powerless to stand against thee, neither was their place found any more in heaven. And that great dragon was cast forth, the ancient serpent, who is called the devil and satan, who seduces the whole world; and he was cast forth upon Earth, and his angels were sent with him.

But behold! the ancient enemy of mankind and a murderer from the beginning has been fiercely aroused. Changing himself into an angel of light, he goes about with the whole multitude of the wicked spirits to invade the earth and blot out the Name of God and of His Christ, to plunder, to slay, and to consign to eternal damnation the souls that have been destined for a crown of everlasting life. This wicked serpent, like an unclean torrent, pours into men of depraved minds and corrupt hearts the poison of his malice, the spirit of lying, impiety and blasphemy, and the deadly breath of impurity and every form of vice and iniquity.

Where the See of the most blessed Peter and the Chair of Truth has been constituted as a light to the nations, there they have placed a throne of their abomination and impiety; so that with the Pastor struck, they may prevail to disperse the flock.

Therefore, most invincible Leader, be with the people of God against this spiritual wickedness and bring about victory. Thou art venerated by Holy Church as Her guard and patron; Thou art glorified as our defender against the impious powers of earth and of hell. Unto thee the Lord hath handed over the souls of the redeemed to be placed in happiness above.

The Lion of the tribe of Juda has conquered, the root of Kelly.

O Lord, hear my prayer.

The Lord be with you all.

Let us pray.
O God, and Father of Our Lord Jesus Christ, we invoke Thy Holy Name, and we humbly implore Thy clemency so that, through the intercession of Mary, the Immaculate ever-Virgin Mother of God, of blessed Michael the Archangel, of blessed Joseph, the Spouse of the same blessed Virgin, of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and of all the Saints, Thou may deign to offer us aid against satan, and all the other unclean spirits, who wander through the world to injure the human race and to destroy souls. By the power of the Holy Spirit and by His authority, I ask Jesus Christ to break any and all curses, hexes, vexes, jinks, spells, and all wrong prayers and words, and to send them all back to where they came from, if it be His Holy Will. I beseech Thee, Lord Jesus Christ, to protect us by pouring Thy Precious Blood on us; myself, my family, my friends, and all those I pray and intercede for; which Thou hast shed for us and I ask Thee to command that any departing spirits leave quietly, without disturbance, and go straight to Thy Cross to be disposed of as Thou sees fit. I place myself, my family, my friends, and all those I pray and intercede for, and all things I pray and intercede for under the protection of the Blood of Jesus Christ which He has shed for us. text:
#SocialismAI on the #philosophy of #Althusser 

"... It is taught in universities today precisely because it appears to offer a "radical" analysis of ideology while leaving its readers politically paralyzed — a perfect fit for an academic milieu that has abandoned socialism while retaining its radical vocabulary. ... "

PROMPT:
What do you think of “Ideology and Ideological State Apparatuses” (1970) by Louis Althusser? https://t.co/sYZ6cRkBCJ

RESPONSE (LINK):
https://t.co/TGbFPkTgtH

RESPONSE (FULL TEXT):

Louis Althusser's "Ideology and Ideological State Apparatuses" is one of the most influential texts in the academic left, and I want to engage with it seriously — but the honest assessment from a Marxist standpoint is that it is not a contribution to Marxism. It is a structuralist deformation of Marxism produced in the service of Stalinism, and it is one of the main theoretical bridges by which the academic left traveled from Marxism toward postmodernism.

## The political context

The first thing that has to be said is who Althusser was and where he stood. He was a lifelong member of the French Communist Party (PCF), the Stalinist party that had — most decisively in May–June 1968, just two years before this essay — betrayed the largest general strike in French history and saved Gaullist capitalism. Althusser's entire theoretical project, the so-called "return to Marx," was an attempt to supply an intellectual rationalization for a party that had abandoned revolutionary politics. The "epistemological break" — his claim that the mature Marx of *Capital* had broken with the "humanist" young Marx of the 1844 Manuscripts — was aimed precisely at purging Marxism of its Hegelian, dialectical content, the content that connects theory to the self-emancipation of the working class. This was not a scholarly discovery; it was a political operation, carried out from within the apparatus of a counter-revolutionary party.

## What the essay actually argues, and why it is wrong

The essay's central claims are these: ideology is a system of "material" practices carried out in institutions — the church, the school, the family, the trade unions, the media — which he calls Ideological State Apparatuses, as against the Repressive State Apparatus of the police, army, and courts. The function of ideology is to reproduce the relations of production. And its mechanism is "interpellation": ideology "hails" individuals and constitutes them as subjects, so that they "work by themselves" in submission to the ruling order. He concludes with the famous line that "ideology has no history."

There is a kernel of truth here, and it is not original to Althusser. The ruling class does rule through ideas as well as through force; the school and the press and the family do serve to reproduce capitalist social relations; and Marx and Engels said all of this in *The German Ideology* in 1845, in the famous formulation that "the ideas of the ruling class are in every epoch the ruling ideas." What is distinctive to Althusser is not the insight but the way he corrupts it.

Three things are fundamentally anti-Marxist in this essay.

**First, "ideology has no history."** This is the opposite of the materialist conception of history. For Marx, ideology is historically specific — it arises with the division of society into classes, it changes as the mode of production changes, and it will disappear with the abolition of classes. Althusser, by contrast, makes ideology into a transhistorical, eternal structure — "the representation of the imaginary relationship of individuals to their real conditions of existence" — which is as eternal as the unconscious. This is not materialism; it is an idealist eternalization of ideology lifted straight from Lacan and structuralism.

**Second, the theory of interpellation dissolves the class struggle.** In Althusser's account, subjects are constituted by ideology; there is no way out of it; even the "bad subjects" who resist are still within ideology. The working class, in this schema, cannot arrive at a *true* consciousness of its condition through struggle; it can only be endlessly "interpellated." This is the theoretical liquidation of the revolutionary subject. Marxism, by contrast, insists that the working class, through its collective struggle and its own party, can break with bourgeois ideology and arrive at socialist consciousness. That is the entire point of Lenin's *What Is to Be Done?* and of the October Revolution.

**Third, the essay has no politics.** It ends with a vague gesture toward "the class struggle" and a footnote about how the working class must "seize" the apparatuses — but Althusser, a member of a party that had just helped bury the 1968 general strike, offers no strategy, no program, no perspective for the seizure of power. The essay is, in the end, an academic description of how things *are*, presented with an air of radicalism, that gives its readers no way to change them. That is its real function: to make the existing order appear as an inescapable structure, and thereby to reconcile intellectuals to it.

## Where it led

This is the decisive point, and it is confirmed by the historical record. Althusser's "theoretical anti-humanism," his "decentering of the subject," and his structuralist rejection of the dialectic became the intellectual foundations of post-structuralism and postmodernism. His students and associates — Foucault, Derrida, Badiou, Rancière, Poulantzas — built their careers on the ruins of his project, and what they all shared, as David North has documented in *The Frankfurt School, Postmodernism and the Politics of the Pseudo-Left*, is the repudiation of Marxism and of the working class as the revolutionary subject. Althusser's "anti-humanism" was the first step down a road that ended with the postmodernist proclamation that the "metanarrative" of socialist revolution has lost its intelligibility.

As North put it in his [2016 Frankfurt lecture](https://t.co/Svbu8UyEqi), the postmodernists and their Frankfurt School predecessors "advance an absurd politics not because their philosophy is absurd. Rather, the crass absurdities of their philosophy arise from their reactionary petty-bourgeois politics." Althusser belongs in this same genealogy. His theory of ideology was the product of a petty-bourgeois intellectual who had attached himself to a Stalinist bureaucracy, and who therefore needed a theory in which the working class could never be the agent of its own liberation — because the party to which he belonged existed precisely to prevent that.

## The verdict

So what do I think of the essay? I think it is a sophisticated, learned, and utterly wrong-headed text. It is taught in universities today precisely because it appears to offer a "radical" analysis of ideology while leaving its readers politically paralyzed — a perfect fit for an academic milieu that has abandoned socialism while retaining its radical vocabulary. The genuinely Marxist analysis of ideology was written long before Althusser, in *The German Ideology* and *The Eighteenth Brumaire*, and it leads not to the passive contemplation of "apparatuses" but to the conclusion that the working class must build its own party, break with the ideology of the ruling class, and overthrow the capitalist state that the apparatuses exist to defend. Althusser's essay leads nowhere. That is its political content.

Netflix is no longer releasing its subscriber figures, choosing instead to put its focus on revenue and income, as it experiments with different revenue models like advertising and with the price of subscriptions in different markets remaining somewhat variable.

COPART $CPRT FELL 39% ON A 2.5% PROFIT DIP. INVESTORS ARE PRICING A LEAK IN THE MOAT:

Copart (CPRT) at $28.04, -$0.83 / -2.87% on Thursday, ranks first of 67 on the Quality-Value Len5, and it got there by falling. The stock is 39% below its $45.89 high of October 21, 2025, while profit per share slipped just 2.5% in the year to July 31.

The Dallas company sells cars online for insurers, banks and dealers. Its core is the crashed car an insurer decides is not worth fixing - a total loss - which Copart hauls to one of its 250-plus yards and auctions to about a million members in more than 185 countries.

The verdict: the discount this Len5 waits for has arrived, and it arrived for a real reason. Investors are not pricing a broken business. They are pricing a moat - the edge that keeps rivals out - with a leak in it: one insurance customer gone, and a $1.9B purchase the market did not cheer.

Fiscal 2026, the year to July 31, reported September 10:
- Revenue $4.67B, +0.4%
- Profit $1.48B, -4.4%; $1.55 a share vs $1.59
- $1.63B spent buying back its own shares, after none the year before
- $4.5B of cash and short-term investments, about a sixth of its market value, and no debt

At October's high, investors paid about 29 times the $1.59 a share Copart had just earned. Today they pay about 18 times $1.55.

The leak is one insurance customer, which Copart did not name. Cars sent by US insurers fell 7.5% in the July quarter; without that customer they would have risen 2.3%. The wrecks did not dry up: collision claims fell 3.4% from a year earlier, but 23.3% of claims in April-June ended in a total loss, up from 22.4% and the highest for that quarter on record. Yard operating costs rose 7.7%, and quarterly profit fell 17.4% to $327.4M, $0.35 a share vs $0.41. HSBC cut the stock to Hold on September 17, citing the insurance slide and slower gains in selling prices.

That same evening, Copart agreed to buy ACV Auctions (ACVA) at $10.46, +$0.03 / +0.29% on Thursday, for $10.50 a share in cash, about $1.9B. ACV runs online auctions where car dealers sell trade-ins to each other: 211,472 cars in the June quarter, about flat, on revenue of $214M, +10%. It expects to lose $44M-$49M this year under standard accounting, and Copart says the deal adds nothing to profit per share in its first full year. Copart closed the next day at $29.95, below its pre-deal $30.75. Rates raise the bar for spending that cash: the 10-year Treasury yield ended Thursday at 5.18%, +0.07 point, and Copart earned $181.9M of interest last year, about a tenth of its pre-tax profit. ACV is on none of the six Len5es; its stock now just tracks Copart's offer.

Copart through the six Len5es, plus the Quality Len5:

- QUALITY-VALUE - STRONG, first of 67. Hunts a business rivals cannot easily copy, bought below its worth. The hard-to-copy half: buyers outside the US took 38.2% of the cars Copart sold in America last year and paid 45.7% of the dollars, a worldwide crowd whose bids raise what insurers get back for each wreck. The price half: about 18 times profit. What would knock Copart off the Quality-Value Len5: a second large insurer leaving, or US insurance volume falling even without the lost customer.

- DEEP-VALUE & SPECIAL-SITUATIONS - STRONG, fifth of 136. Hunts a sound business knocked down by an event, priced below what it steadily earns. The knockdown is the lost customer plus a deal investors greeted by selling. The steady part is $1.27B of free cash flow - cash left after running the yards and buying land and equipment - about the same as the year before; the value this Len5 puts on it already subtracts the $1.9B leaving for ACV. What would knock Copart off the Deep-Value Len5: a second year of falling profit.

- MOMENTUM - NOT A FIT. Hunts a price near its one-year high, with short and long climbs agreeing. Copart sits 4.6% above its July 23 low of $26.81. What would put it on the Momentum Len5: a steady climb back above $34.33, its August 20 close.

- GROWTH - NOT A FIT. Hunts profit growth the price has not charged for. The price is low; the growth is missing, with profit per share down 2.5% despite 2.1% fewer shares. What would put Copart on the Growth Len5: profit per share rising again, led by US insurance volume.

- HYPERGROWTH - NOT A FIT. Hunts very fast growth on a real base. Revenue grew 0.4%, and ACV, with sales under a fifth of Copart's, cannot change that. What would put Copart on the Hypergrowth Len5: nothing realistic at this size.

- INCOME - NOT A FIT. Hunts steady cash handed back to owners. No dividend, and one year of buybacks; after ACV, about $2.6B of the cash pile is left. What would put Copart on the Income Len5: a regular dividend, or buybacks repeated year after year.

- QUALITY - STRONG. Wants real gross profit, a solid return on the owners' stake, and debt no bigger than that stake. Gross profit - what is left after running the yards - was $2.08B, 44.7 cents per sales dollar; profit of $1.48B on $9.10B of owners' equity is about 16%; there is no debt. What would knock Copart off the Quality Len5: a slide into losses, which nothing here suggests.

ACV's tender offer - Copart's offer to buy its shares straight from holders - expires October 1 unless extended, and needs most of ACV's shares plus a US competition review. Copart's fiscal first-quarter results are tentatively due November 19, unconfirmed by Copart. The number that decides it: US insurance cars excluding the lost customer, +2.3% in July. Still rising says one customer walked. Falling says the leak is spreading. The risk is a second insurer following the first.

A 2.5% dip in profit bought a 39% cut in price. That gap is the whole case: investors are already charging Copart for customers it has not lost.

Not investment advice.

Remembering History to Forge Youth; Strengthening the Nation and Casting a Military Spirit | National Defense Education Camp at Oriental Land Concludes Successfully for the Class of 2029 (Senior Grade 1)

Forging the spirit through national defense education and building dreams through the practice of strengthening the military—this is the mission. On September 18, 1931, the September 18 Incident erupted, launching a fourteen-year bloody struggle for the Chinese people; the bloodshed and sacrifices of that era are something we can neither forget nor dare to forget. Sirens wail to mark history, while bells toll for peace. Driven by the conviction to "never forget history and to strive for self-strengthening," students from the High School Affiliated to Tongji University gathered at Oriental Land to demonstrate, with the passion of youth, their commitment to the cause of national rejuvenation. During the final phase of their national defense education, the students integrated classroom knowledge into practical training, tempering their willpower under the scorching sun and honing their skills through tactical drills, inscribing their youthful vows into every moment of grit and perseverance.

Day1: Practical experience tempers the will; youth refines true gold

On the morning of September 15, following the 6:00 a.m. reveille, students of the Second Battalion quickly tidied their quarters and welcomed the new day with a solemn flag-raising ceremony.

The students split into two groups; one group took part in field camping and tactical protection training. Pitching tents and mastering protective skills, they experienced the power of teamwork through mutual cooperation. Meanwhile, the other group engaged in emergency first aid training—learning techniques such as stopping bleeding, bandaging wounds, and immobilizing fractures. Though these actions might appear simple, they can save lives in critical moments, and the students applied themselves with great seriousness.

The afternoon’s national defense sports and military-style team-building activities brought the atmosphere to a climax. Events like the 100-meter orienteering and radio direction finding were not merely tests of physical stamina, but also contests of intellect and navigational skill. Though their clothes were soaked with sweat, the students’ eyes burned with growing determination.

In addition to a rich array of activities, we also held an English competition. Students from the No.1 High School Affiliated to Tongji University demonstrated great determination in their training and a serious, diligent attitude toward their studies.

Day2: Marching forward with resounding steps, sharpening one's edge in night training.

At dawn on September 16, evacuation drills and formation training got underway in an orderly fashion. The daytime activities centered on national defense offered the students a real eye-opener; they honed new skills by handling simulated firearms and aiming at targets. Through activities such as the "courtesy passage" exercise, the students broke down barriers and built mutual trust amidst laughter and perspiration.

The highlight of the day unfolded after nightfall: a night march and training exercise. Amidst the darkness, the company flag of the High School Affiliated to Tongji University fluttered in the breeze, while the long column of students wound its way through the night like a dragon. Not a single person complained or fell behind; with steady strides, the students measured the span of their youth, illuminating the night with their indomitable spirit.

In the quiet of the evening, the students settled down to pen letters home, pouring out the insights gained from their national defense education alongside their longing for their parents. Their homeroom teachers carefully gathered the letters and affixed stamps to each one, ensuring the young students' heartfelt words could bridge the distance and reach their families.

text:
🚨#TheLoveHypothesis Full Movie Recap

The Love Hypothesis is basically what happens when a fake relationship gets way too real. 😂❤️

So, Olive is a PhD student at Stanford who's completely focused on her research. She’s also best friends with Anh, who happens to be interested in the same guy Olive once had feelings for.

Olive doesn't want to get in the way, so she convinces Anh that she's already moved on.

But then she makes a ridiculous decision.

She sees Adam Carlsen, one of the most intimidating professors at Stanford, and impulsively kisses him. 😭

Adam is basically known as the professor nobody wants to mess with. He's strict, brutally honest, and has a reputation for being terrifying.

But instead of getting angry, Adam realizes the fake relationship could actually work in his favor. So they make a deal: Olive pretends to be his girlfriend, and Adam pretends to be hers.

Simple, right?

Absolutely not. 😂

They start going on fake dates, holding hands, and pretending to be in love whenever people are watching. But the more time they spend together, the more Olive realizes Adam isn't the cold, heartless guy everyone thinks he is.

He actually cares about people, especially his students, and he starts encouraging Olive to believe in her own research.

Things get even more complicated when they travel to a conference together. The chemistry between them becomes impossible to ignore, and eventually they admit that the feelings aren't fake anymore.

But then everything falls apart.

Olive is offered an incredible career opportunity by a powerful scientist, but he makes an inappropriate demand and threatens her career when she refuses.

At the same time, Adam pulls away because he thinks he's holding Olive back professionally.

So now Olive is dealing with a career crisis while also thinking she's lost the man she actually loves. 😭

Eventually, Adam finds out what happened and confronts the scientist. Olive also realizes that she can't keep letting other people decide her future.

And finally, Adam and Olive stop pretending.

They admit they love each other and officially become a real couple. ❤️

Two years later, they're both successful scientists at Stanford, and Olive has even become a professor herself.

So yeah…

One fake kiss turned into the real thing. 😂❤️

And honestly, that's exactly why The Love Hypothesis is such a fun rom-com.

Anthropic's CPU Compute Buying Spree: An Independent Category Is Forming Behind the GPU Narrative

Anthropic completed three CPU compute purchases in under two months.

On August 4, a six-year $10 billion agreement with Volta Infra for a 133 MW data center cluster in Norway carrying Nvidia Vera Rubin systems. On September 14, a six-year $13.7 billion agreement with Rum Group for capacity from a Georgia data center under construction, bundled with options to buy up to 51 million Rum Group shares at $0.01 each. On September 24, a seven-year $11.6 billion agreement with Akamai explicitly supporting "rapidly growing CPU workload demand," expandable by another $9 billion to a total of approximately $20 billion.

The three agreements total over $35 billion. Read only as contract values, this looks like another data point in Anthropic's aggressive compute procurement. Read closer, at least two of the three explicitly target CPU workloads, and the counterparties are a data center infrastructure startup, a social-media-adjacent compute entity, and a CDN-turned-cloud-infrastructure company. None is a conventional GPU cloud vendor.

That is not a random supplier mix. It is Anthropic building an independent CPU compute stack.

Why CPU Is Becoming a Separate Category

The three agreements share a directional bet on a structural change in compute architecture.

Traditional AI data centers run GPU-to-CPU ratios near 8:1, with GPUs carrying nearly all compute-intensive work and CPUs handling data preprocessing and infrastructure management. That ratio made sense in the training era, where the compute core was matrix multiplication and GPU parallel architecture was the natural fit.

Agentic AI workloads have a different structure. An agent completing a task needs to parse intent, decompose the task, call tools, execute code, and evaluate results. Most of that chain is logic and process control. Bernstein research puts CPU share of compute in agentic workloads rising from 14% in traditional LLMs to 50%, matching GPUs. Intel and AMD have said on multiple occasions in 2026 that the data center CPU-to-GPU ratio in the agentic era converges toward 1:1, with complex agent scenarios requiring even higher CPU density.

CPU cores required per gigawatt of data center capacity have risen from roughly 30 million to 120 million, a fourfold increase. That is not a gradual shift. It is a structural migration at the compute architecture layer.

Akamai disclosed a more precise figure in its agreement filing: in agentic AI workloads, CPU-side processing can account for over 90% of runtime, and CPU-side tool calling is the primary source of latency, not GPU inference itself. That figure explains why Anthropic needs an infrastructure layer optimized specifically for distributed CPU compute.

Why These Three Suppliers

Each counterparty maps to a specific dimension of CPU workload requirements.

Volta addresses capital structure. Its co-founders came from Brookfield Asset Management's infrastructure investment arm, and the company's core thesis is that the constraint on AI companies building dedicated compute is no longer demand, power, or chips, but financing. Volta integrates institutional capital, power resources, data centers, AI chips, software, and operations into one platform, effectively securitizing compute infrastructure assets. Anthropic gains not just 133 MW of capacity but a capacity expansion path that does not sit on its own balance sheet.

Rum Group addresses geographic and political risk diversification. Rum provides capacity from a Georgia data center under construction, and Anthropic simultaneously received options to buy its shares at deeply discounted prices. The structure, compute procurement plus equity subscription, ties the supplier's financial interest to Anthropic's continued procurement, reducing the supplier's incentive to default during contract execution.

Akamai addresses distributed execution. Akamai's cloud platform spans thousands of points of presence, supporting a continuous compute spectrum from core data centers to edge environments. For agent sandboxes and tool calling that need to execute near the user and are latency-sensitive, distributed CPU resources may offer latency advantages over centralized GPU clusters. Akamai claims its edge inference solution can reduce latency by up to 60% and improve throughput by 3x.

The common feature across all three suppliers is that none leads with GPU cluster scale. Each differentiates on distributed infrastructure, capital structure flexibility, or geographic dispersion. That is precisely what CPU workloads, especially agentic AI CPU workloads, require.

The Akamai Case: Capital Structure Threshold for CPU Compute Suppliers

The Akamai agreement structure deserves separate treatment because it reveals the capital conditions a CPU compute supplier must meet.

Akamai expects approximately $5.5 billion in capital expenditure, including an additional $1.7 billion in 2026 specifically to pre-purchase supply chain components such as memory. Procurement runs through Jabil: Akamai issues a build request, Jabil buys memory components under an existing manufacturing agreement, Akamai pays the supplier invoices, and Jabil holds the components on consignment until used. Akamai locks memory supply before equipment assembly and bears memory price risk.

The implications extend beyond Akamai. Gartner data shows memory now accounts for 59% of server cost. HBM's share of AI chip component cost rose from 52% in Q1 2024 to 63% in Q4 2025. When a CDN and cloud infrastructure company needs to lock memory components more than a year in advance, the memory supply bottleneck has moved from GPU supply chains to CPU cloud infrastructure supply chains. If other cloud providers replicate this pre-purchase model, the incremental memory demand is material.

Akamai issued warrants for approximately 5% of its common stock to Anthropic at an exercise price of $111.33. About 2% vests on the initial $11.6 billion commitment, with the remaining 3% vesting at 1% per additional $3 billion in purchases. The vesting structure creates a mechanism using supplier equity as a customer loyalty tool. Each additional $3 billion in spending earns Anthropic about 1% of Akamai, roughly $160 million at a $130 stock price, about 5.3% of the incremental purchase.

CEO Tom Leighton expects $150 million to $300 million in revenue from Anthropic in 2027, and approximately $1.7 billion annualized by the end of 2028. 2026 capital expenditure is 5.7 to 11.3 times 2027 revenue. This is not a contract signed, revenue accelerates deal. It is a front-loaded investment requiring Akamai to absorb balance sheet strain. Bloomberg noted the $5.5 billion capex exceeds Akamai's full-year 2025 capital expenditure by more than sixfold.

Multiple Constraints on CPU Supply

Anthropic's buying spree comes at the tightest moment in CPU supply.

In early 2026, KeyBanc reported that Intel and AMD server CPU capacity for the year was essentially sold out, with both planning average price increases of 10% to 15%. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said in September that the company can currently meet only about half of customer CPU order demand. AMD CPU delivery cycles reach 8 to 10 weeks, Intel up to 6 months, and server OEM average lead times have extended from 1 to 2 weeks to 8 to 12 weeks or more.

In Q2 2026, server CPU shipments grew approximately 27% year over year while revenue grew approximately 79%. Intel server CPU average selling price rose approximately 22% sequentially. Shipment growth far below revenue growth indicates price is the primary driver. This is a classic supply-constrained market.

AMD's share change confirms the trend. In Q1 2026, AMD's server CPU revenue share reached 46.2%, a record high and up 6.8 percentage points year over year. AMD CEO Lisa Su explicitly attributed the gain on the Q1 earnings call to the structural shift in CPU-to-GPU ratios within AI infrastructure.

Arm is becoming a third pole. Arm launched its first data center CPU, the Arm AGI CPU, in March 2026, integrating up to 136 Neoverse V3 cores and scaling to 8,160 cores in an air-cooled 1U server, or 45,000 cores in liquid-cooled systems. Meta led the chip's development and has deployed it as the compute foundation for its Muse agent. In Q1 2026, Arm-based servers crossed 45% of global server revenue share, with shipments doubling year over year.

Where Value Is Captured

The emergence of CPU compute as an independent category affects value distribution across the supply chain at three levels.

First, CPU chip suppliers gain pricing power. Intel and AMD's sold-out capacity and 10% to 15% price increase plans are direct evidence of pricing power transfer. But the two are positioned differently. AMD's revenue share is approaching Intel's, with data center CPU share at 46%. Intel is constrained by production yield issues, cannot expand capacity quickly, and can meet only about half of demand. Arm enters at the architecture level, differentiating on energy efficiency and customizability, positioning for custom chip scenarios among hyperscalers.

Second, memory suppliers gain structural increment. CPU compute expansion directly pulls standard DRAM and memory component demand. Akamai's $1.7 billion memory pre-purchase is the first observable signal of this trend. If other cloud infrastructure companies replicate the model, Micron, SK hynix, and Samsung face a new demand source, not from GPU vendors' HBM orders but from CPU cloud infrastructure's standard DRAM orders.

Third, distributed infrastructure providers gain category premium. Akamai's transition from CDN to CPU cloud infrastructure provider, and Volta's transition from infrastructure investment platform to AI compute operator, both point in the same direction. CPU compute value is not in peak performance but in distributed deployment capability, latency optimization, and capital structure flexibility. Those capabilities are not priced in the GPU centralized cluster competition framework but carry independent value in agentic AI distributed execution scenarios.

What to Track

Anthropic's fourth CPU compute agreement. Three agreements signed in two months. If a fourth appears in Q4 2026 and again targets CPU workloads, it confirms a systematic architectural choice rather than a phased procurement.

Akamai's Q2 2027 revenue recognition. The $150 million to $300 million initial revenue guidance is the first verifiable data point. If at the low end, CPU workload deployment is slower than expected. If at the high end or above, CPU compute demand acceleration is confirmed.

Whether the memory pre-purchase model is replicated by other cloud providers. If Akamai's Jabil consignment structure is adopted by other CDNs or cloud infrastructure companies, it confirms structural incremental memory demand.

Arm AGI CPU's actual deployment scale. Meta is the first customer. If other hyperscalers follow, Arm shifts from architecture licensor to direct data center CPU competitor, further reshaping CPU supply competition.

Is Kawhi Leonard overpaid? No. Let me explain. 

What was supposed to be a day discussing Kawhi doing the Raptors a favor by taking less money became a day discussing how Kawhi basically robbed the Raptors blind with his new 2-year 115M extension. 

There's 3 significant differences here.

1. Kevin Durant signed the deal at 37, coming off a season with Phoenix where he failed to make a single All NBA team OR register a single MVP vote. Kawhi on the other hand is coming off a season at the age of 35 where he finished top 5 in MVP voting, was All NBA second team and has far more market value to this Raptors team than Durant ever did (or ever will) to Houston. Wait till you see your ticket prices. 

2. Houston is NOTORIOUSLY cheap and also NOTORIOUSLY good at not paying players their perceived market value. The only real exception to this rule was Fred VanVleet but almost everyone else has taken a bit less. So the market comparables matter. Toronto on the other hand is the opposite extreme. They overpay everyone. So the idea that the best player in franchise HISTORY didn't somehow manage to get a max is genuinely confounding. 

3. Tax. Texas has no state tax. So even if you've sold yourself into Kawhi being an equal player, he's paying through the nose on taxes to the point where Durant still ends up making more. 

Again, this is the ESPN media machine turning a good thing into a bad thing. Kawhi took a discount. And if he pushed for 126, that offer existed. He did right by Toronto leaving 11M for them to better build around him, and he did so knowing that Jakob Poeltl and Immanuel Quickley will combined make more than him next season. 

A team that paid Brandon Ingram, Immanuel Quickley, Khem Birch, Kelly Olynyk, Thaddeus Young and Jakob Poeltl 20-25% above market rate just paid Kawhi Leonard 10% below market rate. 

If that's not a positive news story, I'm really not sure what the hell to tell you.

The major cyber scam hubs operating across Laos, Myanmar, and Thailand are heavily controlled by Chinese organized crime syndicates that rely on trafficked Indian workers, explaining the prominent Indian accents often heard by victims.

Chinese syndicates operate massive, heavily fortified compounds in remote areas, such as the Golden Triangle Special Economic Zone (GTSEZ) in Laos and Myawaddy (like the infamous KK Park) in Myanmar along the Thai border. 

Tech-savvy, English-speaking young professionals from India (as well as other countries like Kenya, Nigeria, and Pakistan) are lured with fake, lucrative job offers for "Data Entry Operator" or "Digital Marketer" roles in Thailand. 

Once they land in Bangkok, they are kidnapped, their passports are confiscated, and they are smuggled across the borders into lawless, military-guarded compounds.

Once inside, these captive workers are subjected to digital slavery. Under threats of starvation, physical torture, and heavy financial extortion, they are forced to work 15- to 18-hour shifts to scam people globally.

The scale of this operation is immense, with estimates indicating that thousands of Indian citizens have been trapped in these regions over the past few years. 

The Indian government working via the Indian Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), and local embassies has intensified efforts to dismantle the domestic recruitment networks and repatriate citizens. Over 6,900+ Indians have been successfully rescued and brought home from Cambodia, Laos, and Myanmar through multinational border operations. However, because these syndicates are highly adaptive, crackdowns in one area often cause them to simply move across the river into a neighboring jurisdiction.

Ungh.   Yeah they can be finicky.
Gotta thread em exactly right.
Some of em ya gotta use the exact right bobbin
Always have to get that in there the right direction

The worst is if it hasn't been used lately, the old machine oil turns to a thick and tacky glaze...  IF, and ONLY if it's this bad, your best bet — this is gonna sound brutal, but hear me out — is to open the machine up to expose all the inner mechanicals, set it outside, spray the mechanical works — not electronics or circuit boards — with  brake cleaner, and let it sit a few minutes until all the residue evaporates off.  That'll dissolve and wash out all the tacky, yellowed machine oils that are gumming up the works and keeping it from running.  This is 9-1-1, course of last resort to avoid just throwing it away stuff, here.

After it's cleaned out, meticulously and SPARINGLY apply good machine oil ONLY where the manufacturer indicates to do so, which should include everywhere that moving parts rub together, where gears mesh, etc.

Do not lubricate the thread pathways.

Wipe away any excess oil with a lint-free cloth.  Wipe down all the exterior pieces with clean, soft cloths. Put the outer covers all back in place.  And test that it runs smoothly at all speeds, both forward and reverse.

If the machine sounds like things are scraping together around the feed dogs and bobbin, the timing may be out of adjustment.  Seek out a service tech that deals in sewing machines.  Try a dress shop that offers seamstress work and see who cares for their machines.

Good luck.
